The source can be checked out anonymously from Subversion with this command:

```bash
$ svn checkout http://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/trunk/tooling/maven/maven-jspc-plugin jspc-maven-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-1-0-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>Developer Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-1-0-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/trunk/tooling/maven/maven-jspc-plugin jspc-maven-plugin
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password):

```bash
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-1-0-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>Access from Behind a Firewall

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-1-0-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/trunk/tooling/maven/maven-jspc-plugin jspc-maven-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-1-0-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>Access Through a Proxy

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-1-0-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```text
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-0-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling JSPC Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| jspc:help | Display help information on jspc-maven-plugin.Callmvn jspc:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| jspc:jspc | TheJspcMojois implements the Sling Maven JspC goaljspccompiling JSP into the target and creating a component descriptor for Declarative Services to use the JSP with the help of the appropriate adapter as component. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.8 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>jspc-maven-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>2.2.0</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>jspc-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.2.0</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-2-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling JSPC Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-2-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-2-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| jspc:help | Display help information on jspc-maven-plugin.Callmvn jspc:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| jspc:jspc | TheJspcMojois implements the Sling Maven JspC goaljspccompiling JSP into the target and creating a component descriptor for Declarative Services to use the JSP with the help of the appropriate adapter as component. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-2-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-2-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.7 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-2-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-2-2-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>jspc-maven-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>2.2.2</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>jspc-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.2.2</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling JSPC Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| jspc:help | Display help information on jspc-maven-plugin.Callmvn jspc:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| jspc:jspc | TheJspcMojois implements the Sling Maven JspC goaljspccompiling JSP into the target and creating a component descriptor for Declarative Services to use the JSP with the help of the appropriate adapter as component. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.5.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.7 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>jspc-maven-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>2.3.0</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>jspc-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.3.0</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-index"></a>

# Apache Sling JSPC Maven Plugin –

The Apache Sling JSPC Maven Plugin Compiles JSP scripts into class files.

See [Goals](#sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info) for a list of supported goals.

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-index--Overview"></a>Overview

The JSPC Maven Plugin provides a single goal `jspc` which is by default executed in the `compile` phase of the Maven build process. This goal takes all JSP source files from a configured location (`src/main/scripts` by default) and compiles them into classes in a configurable location (`target/classes` by default).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-index--Usage"></a>Usage

To use the JSPC Maven Plugin define the following elements in the `<plugins>` section of the POM:

```xml
<project>    ....    <build>        ....        <plugins>            ....            <plugin>                <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>                <artifactId>jspc-maven-plugin</artifactId>                <version>2.3.4</version>                <executions>                    <execution>                        <id>compile-jsp</id>                        <goals>                            <goal>jspc</goal>                        </goals>                    </execution>                </executions>            </plugin>            ....        <plugins>        ....    <build>    ....<project>
```

The generated JSP classes are automatically copied to the generated bundle jar file if the Maven Bundle Plugin is used to build the project package.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling JSPC Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| jspc:help | Display help information on jspc-maven-plugin.Callmvn jspc:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| jspc:jspc | TheJspcMojois implements the Sling Maven JspC goaljspccompiling JSP into the target and creating a component descriptor for Declarative Services to use the JSP with the help of the appropriate adapter as component. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.5.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.7 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-archives-jspc-maven-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>  ...  <build>    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->    <pluginManagement>      <plugins>        <plugin>          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>          <artifactId>jspc-maven-plugin</artifactId>          <version>2.3.4</version>        </plugin>        ...      </plugins>    </pluginManagement>    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->    <plugins>      <plugin>        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>        <artifactId>jspc-maven-plugin</artifactId>        <version>2.3.4</version>      </plugin>      ...    </plugins>  </build>  ...</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

# Apache Sling JSPC Maven Plugin – jspc:help

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-help-mojo--jspc:help"></a>jspc:help

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:jspc-maven-plugin:2.3.4:help

**Description**:

Display help information on jspc-maven-plugin.  
Call `mvn jspc:help -Ddetail=true
-Dgoal=<goal-name>` to display parameter details.

**Attributes**:

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-help-mojo--Optional_Parameters"></a>Optional Parameters

| Name | Type | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <detail> | boolean | - | Iftrue, display all settable properties for each goal.Default value is:false.User property is:detail. |
| <goal> | String | - | The name of the goal for which to show help. If unspecified, all goals will be displayed.User property is:goal. |
| <indentSize> | int | - | The number of spaces per indentation level, should be positive.Default value is:2.User property is:indentSize. |
| <lineLength> | int | - | The maximum length of a display line, should be positive.Default value is:80.User property is:lineLength. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-help-mojo--Parameter_Details"></a>Parameter Details

If `true`, display all settable properties for each
goal.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `detail`
- **Default**: `false`

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-help-mojo--a.3Cgoal.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-help-mojo--goal"></a><goal>**

The name of the goal for which to show help. If unspecified, all
goals will be displayed.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `goal`

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-help-mojo--a.3CindentSize.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-help-mojo--indentSize"></a><indentSize>**

The number of spaces per indentation level, should be positive.

- **Type**: `int`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `indentSize`
- **Default**: `2`

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-help-mojo--a.3ClineLength.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-help-mojo--lineLength"></a><lineLength>**

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-jspc-mojo"></a>

# Apache Sling JSPC Maven Plugin – jspc:jspc

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-jspc-mojo--jspc:jspc"></a>jspc:jspc

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:jspc-maven-plugin:2.3.4:jspc

**Description**:

The `JspcMojo` is implements the Sling Maven JspC goal
`jspc` compiling JSP into the target and creating a
component descriptor for Declarative Services to use the JSP with
the help of the appropriate adapter as component.

**Attributes**:

- Requires a Maven project to be executed.
- Requires dependency resolution of artifacts in scope: `compile`.
- Binds by default to the [lifecycle phase](http://maven.apache.org/ref/current/maven-core/lifecycles.html): `compile`.

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-jspc-mojo--Optional_Parameters"></a>Optional Parameters

| Name | Type | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <compilerSourceVM> | String | - | The Compiler Source Version of the Java source generated from the JSP files before compiling into classes.Default value is:1.8.User property is:jspc.compilerSourceVM. |
| <compilerTargetVM> | String | - | The Target Virtual Machine Version to generate class files for.Default value is:1.8.User property is:jspc.compilerTargetVM. |
| <excludes> | String[] | - | Excluded JSPs, empty by default |
| <failOnError> | boolean | - | (no description)Default value is:true.User property is:jspc.failOnError. |
| <feature> | JspcMojo$FeatureDependency | - | (no description) |
| <generateCompilationReport> | boolean | 2.3.0 | Generates a compilation report text file (compilation_report.json) in the${project.build.outputDirectory}.The compilation report has the following format:{         "packageProviders": [             {                 "package": "<a Java package name>",                 "providers": [                     "<Maven Artifact ID>"                 ]             }         ],         "jspDependencies": [             {                 "jsp": "src/main/scripts/<a script>.jsp",                 "dependencies": [                     "<jar file name>:<path to JSP>",                     "src/main/scripts/<path to file in local project>.jsp"                 ]             }         ],         "unusedDependencies": [             "<Maven Artifact ID>"         ]      }Default value is:false.User property is:jspc.generateCompilationReport. |
| <includes> | String[] | - | Included JSPs, defaults to"**/*.jsp" |
| <jasperClassDebugInfo> | boolean | - | (no description)Default value is:true.User property is:jspc.jasper.classdebuginfo. |
| <jasperEnablePooling> | boolean | - | (no description)Default value is:true.User property is:jspc.jasper.enablePooling. |
| <jasperGenStringAsCharArray> | boolean | - | (no description)Default value is:false.User property is:jspc.jasper.genStringAsCharArray. |
| <jasperIeClassId> | String | - | (no description)Default value is:clsid:8AD9C840-044E-11D1-B3E9-00805F499D93.User property is:jspc.jasper.ieClassId. |
| <jasperKeepGenerated> | boolean | - | (no description)Default value is:true.User property is:jspc.jasper.keepgenerated. |
| <jasperMappedFile> | boolean | - | (no description)Default value is:true.User property is:jspc.jasper.mappedfile. |
| <jasperSuppressSmap> | boolean | - | (no description)Default value is:false.User property is:jspc.jasper.suppressSmap. |
| <jasperTrimSpaces> | boolean | - | (no description)Default value is:false.User property is:jspc.jasper.trimSpaces. |
| <jspFileExtensions> | String | - | Deprecated.Use theincludesfilter instead.Default value is:jsp,jspx.User property is:jspc.jspFileExtensions. |
| <outputDirectory> | String | - | Target directory for the compiled JSP classes.Default value is:${project.build.outputDirectory}.User property is:jspc.outputDirectory. |
| <printCompilationReport> | boolean | - | Prints a compilation report by listing all the packages and dependencies that were used during processing the JSPs.Default value is:false.User property is:jspc.printCompilationReport. |
| <resourceDirectories> | File[] | - | List of alternative resource directories used during compiling. |
| <servletPackage> | String | - | When defined, this will set the value for theConstants.JSP_PACKAGE_NAME_PROPERTY_NAMEsystem property of the Jasper compiler, which defines the prefix package under which compiled JSPs will be generated.User property is:jspc.servletPackage. |
| <showSuccess> | boolean | - | (no description)Default value is:false.User property is:jspc.showSuccess. |
| <sourceDirectory> | File | - | Location of the JSP source file.Default value is:${project.build.scriptSourceDirectory}.User property is:jspc.sourceDirectory. |

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-jspc-mojo--a.3CgenerateCompilationReport.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-jspc-maven-plugin-jspc-mojo--generateCompilationReport"></a><generateCompilationReport>**

Generates a compilation report text file (compilation\_report.json)
in the `${project.build.outputDirectory`}.

The compilation report has the following format:

```json
    {
        "packageProviders": [
            {
                "package": "<a Java package name>",
                "providers": [
                    "<Maven Artifact ID>"
                ]
            }
        ],
        "jspDependencies": [
            {
                "jsp": "src/main/scripts/<a script>.jsp",
                "dependencies": [
                    "<jar file name>:<path to JSP>",
                    "src/main/scripts/<path to file in local project>.jsp"
                ]
            }
        ],
        "unusedDependencies": [
            "<Maven Artifact ID>"
        ]
     }
   
```

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Since**: `2.3.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `jspc.generateCompilationReport`
- **Default**: `false`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling Maven Plugin for Supporting Bundle Development – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| sling:deploy | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle. This method posts the bundle built by maven to an OSGi Bundle Repository accepting the bundle. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:deploy-file | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle. This method posts the bundle built by maven to an OSGi Bundle Repository accepting the bundle. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:generate-adapter-metadata | Build Adapter Metadata from Annotated Classes |
| sling:help | Display help information on maven-sling-plugin.Callmvn sling:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| sling:install | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. |
| sling:install-file | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. |
| sling:uninstall | Uninstall an OSGi bundle from a running Sling instance. |
| sling:validate | Plugin to validate resources: - validate json files |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.0.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.7 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>2.1.10</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.1.10</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Overview"></a>Overview

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Overview"></a>

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at [http://svnbook.red-bean.com/](http://svnbook.red-bean.com/).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Web_Browser_Access"></a>Web Browser Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Web_Browser_Access"></a>

The following is a link to a browsable version of the source repository:

```text

```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Anonymous_Access"></a>Anonymous Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Anonymous_Access"></a>

The source can be checked out anonymously from Subversion with this command:

```bash
$ svn checkout http://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.1.10 maven-sling-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>Developer Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.1.10 maven-sling-plugin
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password):

```bash
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>Access from Behind a Firewall

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.1.10 maven-sling-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>Access Through a Proxy

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-1-10-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```text
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling Maven Sling Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| sling:deploy | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle built by maven to the OSGi Bundle Repository. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:deploy-file | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle referenced viasling.fileto an OSGi Bundle Repository accepting the bundle. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:fsmount | Creates OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. |
| sling:fsunmount | Removes OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. |
| sling:generate-adapter-metadata | Buildadapter metadata (JSON)for the Web Console Plugin at/system/console/status-adaptersand/system/console/adaptersfrom classes annotated withadapter annotations. |
| sling:help | Display help information on maven-sling-plugin.Callmvn sling:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| sling:install | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. The plugin places an HTTP POST request toFelix Web Console. It's also possible to HTTP PUT instead of POST leveraging theWebDAV bundle from Sling. Since version 2.1.8 you can also leverage the theSling POST servletfor that The chosen method depends on the parameterdeploymentMethod.Intermediate Node CreationFor alldeploymentMethods except WebDAV the bundle is not directly deployed within the OSGi container, but rather being uploaded to the JCR and from there on being picked up by theJCR Installer Providerasynchronously, which takes care of deploying it in the OSGi container. For both other deployment methods, intermediate nodes (i.e. inexisting parent nodes) are automatically created. The primary type of those intermediate nodes depend on the deployment method.WebDAV, uses the configured collection node type, by defaultsling:Folder(see alsoWebDAV Configuration)SlingPostServlet, uses internallyResourceResolverFactory.create(...)without setting anyjcr:primaryType. Therefore theJcrResourceProviderFactorywill callNode.addNode(String relPath)which determines a fitting node type automatically, depending on the parents node type definition (seeJavadoc). So in most of the cases this should be asling:Folder, as this is the first allowed child node definition insling:Folder. This only may differ, if your existing parent node is not of typesling:Folderitself. |
| sling:install-file | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. |
| sling:uninstall | Uninstall an OSGi bundle from a running Sling instance. The plugin places by default an HTTP POST request toFelix Web Consoleto uninstall the bundle. It's also possible to use HTTP DELETE leveraging theWebDAV bundle from Sling. or theSling POST servletto uninstall the bundle. The chosen method depends on the parameterdeploymentMethod. |
| sling:validate | Thevalidategoal checks the JSON code of a bundle. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.0.4 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.7 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>2.3.0</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.3.0</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

# Apache Sling Maven Sling Plugin – Source Code Management

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Overview"></a>Overview

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Overview"></a>

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at [http://svnbook.red-bean.com/](http://svnbook.red-bean.com/).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Web_Browser_Access"></a>Web Browser Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Web_Browser_Access"></a>

The following is a link to a browsable version of the source repository:

```text
http://svn.apache.org/viewvc/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.0
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Anonymous_Access"></a>Anonymous Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Anonymous_Access"></a>

The source can be checked out anonymously from Subversion with this command:

```bash
$ svn checkout http://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.0 maven-sling-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>Developer Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.0 maven-sling-plugin
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password):

```bash
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>Access from Behind a Firewall

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.0 maven-sling-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>Access Through a Proxy

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-0-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```text
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling Maven Sling Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| sling:deploy | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle built by maven to the OSGi Bundle Repository. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:deploy-file | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle referenced viasling.fileto an OSGi Bundle Repository accepting the bundle. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:fsmount | Creates OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. |
| sling:fsunmount | Removes OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. |
| sling:generate-adapter-metadata | Buildadapter metadata (JSON)for the Web Console Plugin at/system/console/status-adaptersand/system/console/adaptersfrom classes annotated withadapter annotations. |
| sling:help | Display help information on maven-sling-plugin.Callmvn sling:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| sling:install | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. The plugin places an HTTP POST request toFelix Web Console. It's also possible to HTTP PUT instead of POST leveraging theWebDAV bundle from Sling. Since version 2.1.8 you can also leverage the theSling POST servletfor that The chosen method depends on the parameterdeploymentMethod.Intermediate Node CreationFor alldeploymentMethods except WebDAV the bundle is not directly deployed within the OSGi container, but rather being uploaded to the JCR and from there on being picked up by theJCR Installer Providerasynchronously, which takes care of deploying it in the OSGi container. For both other deployment methods, intermediate nodes (i.e. inexisting parent nodes) are automatically created. The primary type of those intermediate nodes depend on the deployment method.WebDAV, uses the configured collection node type, by defaultsling:Folder(see alsoWebDAV Configuration)SlingPostServlet, uses internallyResourceResolverFactory.create(...)without setting anyjcr:primaryType. Therefore theJcrResourceProviderFactorywill callNode.addNode(String relPath)which determines a fitting node type automatically, depending on the parents node type definition (seeJavadoc). So in most of the cases this should be asling:Folder, as this is the first allowed child node definition insling:Folder. This only may differ, if your existing parent node is not of typesling:Folderitself. |
| sling:install-file | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. |
| sling:uninstall | Uninstall an OSGi bundle from a running Sling instance. The plugin places by default an HTTP POST request toFelix Web Consoleto uninstall the bundle. It's also possible to use HTTP DELETE leveraging theWebDAV bundle from Sling. or theSling POST servletto uninstall the bundle. The chosen method depends on the parameterdeploymentMethod. |
| sling:validate | Thevalidategoal checks the JSON code of a bundle. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.0.4 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.7 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>2.3.2</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.3.2</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

# Apache Sling Maven Sling Plugin – Source Code Management

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Overview"></a>Overview

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Overview"></a>

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at [http://svnbook.red-bean.com/](http://svnbook.red-bean.com/).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Web_Browser_Access"></a>Web Browser Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Web_Browser_Access"></a>

The following is a link to a browsable version of the source repository:

```text

```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Anonymous_Access"></a>Anonymous Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Anonymous_Access"></a>

The source can be checked out anonymously from Subversion with this command:

```bash
$ svn checkout http://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.2 maven-sling-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>Developer Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.2 maven-sling-plugin
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password):

```bash
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>Access from Behind a Firewall

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.2 maven-sling-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>Access Through a Proxy

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-2-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```text
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling Maven Sling Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| sling:deploy | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle built by maven to the OSGi Bundle Repository. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:deploy-file | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle referenced viasling.fileto an OSGi Bundle Repository accepting the bundle. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:fsmount | Creates OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. |
| sling:fsunmount | Removes OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. |
| sling:generate-adapter-metadata | Buildadapter metadata (JSON)for the Web Console Plugin at/system/console/status-adaptersand/system/console/adaptersfrom classes annotated withadapter annotations. |
| sling:help | Display help information on maven-sling-plugin.Callmvn sling:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| sling:install | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. The plugin places an HTTP POST request toFelix Web Console. It's also possible to HTTP PUT instead of POST leveraging theWebDAV bundle from Sling. Since version 2.1.8 you can also leverage the theSling POST servletfor that The chosen method depends on the parameterdeploymentMethod.Intermediate Node CreationFor alldeploymentMethods except WebDAV the bundle is not directly deployed within the OSGi container, but rather being uploaded to the JCR and from there on being picked up by theJCR Installer Providerasynchronously, which takes care of deploying it in the OSGi container. For both other deployment methods, intermediate nodes (i.e. inexisting parent nodes) are automatically created. The primary type of those intermediate nodes depend on the deployment method.WebDAV, uses the configured collection node type, by defaultsling:Folder(see alsoWebDAV Configuration)SlingPostServlet, uses internallyResourceResolverFactory.create(...)without setting anyjcr:primaryType. Therefore theJcrResourceProviderFactorywill callNode.addNode(String relPath)which determines a fitting node type automatically, depending on the parents node type definition (seeJavadoc). So in most of the cases this should be asling:Folder, as this is the first allowed child node definition insling:Folder. This only may differ, if your existing parent node is not of typesling:Folderitself. |
| sling:install-file | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. |
| sling:uninstall | Uninstall an OSGi bundle from a running Sling instance. The plugin places by default an HTTP POST request toFelix Web Consoleto uninstall the bundle. It's also possible to use HTTP DELETE leveraging theWebDAV bundle from Sling. or theSling POST servletto uninstall the bundle. The chosen method depends on the parameterdeploymentMethod. |
| sling:validate | Thevalidategoal checks the JSON code of a bundle. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.0.4 |

| JDK | 1.7 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>2.3.4</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.3.4</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

# Apache Sling Maven Sling Plugin – Source Code Management

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Overview"></a>Overview

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Overview"></a>

This project uses [Subversion](http://subversion.apache.org/) to manage its source code. Instructions on Subversion use can be found at [http://svnbook.red-bean.com/](http://svnbook.red-bean.com/).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Web_Browser_Access"></a>Web Browser Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Web_Browser_Access"></a>

The following is a link to a browsable version of the source repository:

```text
http://svn.apache.org/viewvc/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.4
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Anonymous_Access"></a>Anonymous Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Anonymous_Access"></a>

The source can be checked out anonymously from Subversion with this command:

```bash
$ svn checkout http://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.4 maven-sling-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>Developer Access

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Developer_Access"></a>

Everyone can access the Subversion repository via HTTP, but committers must checkout the Subversion repository via HTTPS.

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.4 maven-sling-plugin
```

To commit changes to the repository, execute the following command to commit your changes (svn will prompt you for your password):

```bash
$ svn commit --username your-username -m "A message"
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>Access from Behind a Firewall

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Access_from_Behind_a_Firewall"></a>

For those users who are stuck behind a corporate firewall which is blocking HTTP access to the Subversion repository, you can try to access it via the developer connection:

```bash
$ svn checkout https://svn.apache.org/repos/asf/sling/tags/maven-sling-plugin-2.3.4 maven-sling-plugin
```

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>Access Through a Proxy

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-4-source-repository--Access_Through_a_Proxy"></a>

The Subversion client can go through a proxy, if you configure it to do so. First, edit your "servers" configuration file to indicate which proxy to use. The file's location depends on your operating system. On Linux or Unix it is located in the directory "~/.subversion". On Windows it is in "%APPDATA%\Subversion". (Try "echo %APPDATA%", note this is a hidden directory.)

There are comments in the file explaining what to do. If you don't have that file, get the latest Subversion client and run any command; this will cause the configuration directory and template files to be created.

Example: Edit the 'servers' file and add something like:

```text
[global]
http-proxy-host = your.proxy.name
http-proxy-port = 3128
```

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-8-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling Maven Sling Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-8-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-8-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| sling:deploy | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle built by maven to the OSGi Bundle Repository. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:deploy-file | Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle referenced viasling.fileto an OSGi Bundle Repository accepting the bundle. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:fsmount | Creates OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. |
| sling:fsunmount | Removes OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. |
| sling:generate-adapter-metadata | Buildadapter metadata (JSON)for the Web Console Plugin at/system/console/status-adaptersand/system/console/adaptersfrom classes annotated withadapter annotations. |
| sling:help | Display help information on maven-sling-plugin.Callmvn sling:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| sling:install | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. The plugin places an HTTP POST request toFelix Web Console. It's also possible to HTTP PUT instead of POST leveraging theWebDAV bundle from Sling. Since version 2.1.8 you can also leverage the theSling POST servletfor that The chosen method depends on the parameterdeploymentMethod.Intermediate Node CreationFor alldeploymentMethods except WebDAV the bundle is not directly deployed within the OSGi container, but rather being uploaded to the JCR and from there on being picked up by theJCR Installer Providerasynchronously, which takes care of deploying it in the OSGi container. For both other deployment methods, intermediate nodes (i.e. inexisting parent nodes) are automatically created. The primary type of those intermediate nodes depend on the deployment method.WebDAV, uses the configured collection node type, by defaultsling:Folder(see alsoWebDAV Configuration)SlingPostServlet, uses internallyResourceResolverFactory.create(...)without setting anyjcr:primaryType. Therefore theJcrResourceProviderFactorywill callNode.addNode(String relPath)which determines a fitting node type automatically, depending on the parents node type definition (seeJavadoc). So in most of the cases this should be asling:Folder, as this is the first allowed child node definition insling:Folder. This only may differ, if your existing parent node is not of typesling:Folderitself. |
| sling:install-file | Install an OSGi bundle to a running Sling instance. |
| sling:uninstall | Uninstall an OSGi bundle from a running Sling instance. The plugin places by default an HTTP POST request toFelix Web Consoleto uninstall the bundle. It's also possible to use HTTP DELETE leveraging theWebDAV bundle from Sling. or theSling POST servletto uninstall the bundle. The chosen method depends on the parameterdeploymentMethod. |
| sling:validate | Thevalidategoal checks the JSON code of a bundle. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-8-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-8-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-maven-sling-plugin-archives-maven-sling-plugin-2-3-8-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>2.3.8</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-sling-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.3.8</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo"></a>

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – scriptingbundle:metadata

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--scriptingbundle:metadata"></a>scriptingbundle:metadata

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:scriptingbundle-maven-plugin:0.2.0:metadata

**Description**:

The metadata goal will generate two Maven project
properties, namely
org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability
and
org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability
which can be used to generate the corresponding OSGi bundle headers
for bundles providing scripts executable by a
ScriptEngine.

**Attributes**:

- Requires a Maven project to be executed.
- Binds by default to the [lifecycle phase](http://maven.apache.org/ref/current/maven-core/lifecycles.html): prepare-package.

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--Optional_Parameters"></a>Optional Parameters

| Name | Type | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <excludes> | String[] | 0.2.0 | Allows defining a list of excluded files and folders or patterns to filter which files should be excluded in the analysis for generating capabilities.The following list provides the default excluded files and patterns:Miscellaneous typical temporary files**/*~, **/#*#, **/.#*, **/%*%, **/._*CVS**/CVS, **/CVS/**, **/.cvsignoreSubversion**/.svn, **/.svn/**Bazaar**/.bzr, **/.bzr/**Mac**/.DS_StoreMercurial**/.hg, **/.hg/**git**/.git, **/.git/**User property is:scriptingbundle.excludes. |
| <includes> | String[] | 0.2.0 | Allows defining a list of included files and folders or patterns to filter which files should be included in the analysis for generating capabilities. By default all files are included.Default value is:**.User property is:scriptingbundle.includes. |
| <scriptEngineMappings> | Map | 0.2.0 | Allows overriding the default extension to script engine mapping, in order to correctly generate thesling.resourceType;scriptEngineProvide-Capabilityattribute value. When configuring this mapping, please make sure to use the script extension as the key and one of the Script Engine's name (obtained fromScriptEngineFactory.getNames()) as the value.The following list represents the default extension to Script Engine mapping:ftlfreemarkergstgstringhtmlhtljavajavaesp, ecmarhinojsp, jspf, jspxjsp |
| <searchPaths> | Set | 0.2.0 | Allows overriding the default search paths (/appsand/libs). When scripts are organised in folders which follow the search path structure, the Mojo will generate two resource types for each resource type folder. For example:src/main/scripts/apps/org/apache/sling/example/example.htmlwill generate the following two resource typesorg/apache/sling/example     /apps/org/apache/sling/exampleHowever, the following scriptsrc/main/scripts/org/apache/sling/example/example.htmlwill generate only one resource typeorg/apache/sling/exampleUser property is:scriptingbundle.searchPaths. |
| <sourceDirectories> | Set | 0.2.0 | Defines where this goal will look for scripts in the project. By default thesrc/main/scriptsandsrc/main/resources/javax.scriptfolders will be considered.User property is:scriptingbundle.sourceDirectories. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--Parameter_Details"></a>Parameter Details

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--a.3Cexcludes.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--excludes"></a><excludes>**

Allows defining a list of excluded files and folders or patterns to
filter which files should be excluded in the analysis for
generating capabilities.

The following list provides the default excluded files and
patterns:

- Miscellaneous typical temporary files\*\*/\*~, \*\*/#\*#, \*\*/.#\*, \*\*/%\*%, \*\*/.\_\*
- CVS\*\*/CVS, \*\*/CVS/\*\*, \*\*/.cvsignore
- Subversion\*\*/.svn, \*\*/.svn/\*\*
- Bazaar\*\*/.bzr, \*\*/.bzr/\*\*
- Mac\*\*/.DS\_Store
- Mercurial\*\*/.hg, \*\*/.hg/\*\*
- git\*\*/.git, \*\*/.git/\*\*

- **Type**: java.lang.String[]
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No
- **User Property**: scriptingbundle.excludes

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--a.3Cincludes.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--includes"></a><includes>**

Allows defining a list of included files and folders or patterns to
filter which files should be included in the analysis for
generating capabilities. By default all files are included.

- **Type**: java.lang.String[]
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No
- **User Property**: scriptingbundle.includes
- **Default**: \*\*

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--a.3CscriptEngineMappings.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--scriptEngineMappings"></a><scriptEngineMappings>**

Allows overriding the default extension to script engine mapping,
in order to correctly generate the
sling.resourceType;scriptEngine
Provide-Capability attribute value. When configuring
this mapping, please make sure to use the script extension as the
key and one of the Script Engine's name (obtained from
ScriptEngineFactory.getNames()) as the value.

The following list represents the default extension to Script
Engine mapping:

- ftlfreemarker
- gstgstring
- htmlhtl
- javajava
- esp, ecmarhino
- jsp, jspf, jspxjsp

- **Type**: java.util.Map
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--a.3CsearchPaths.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--searchPaths"></a><searchPaths>**

Allows overriding the default search paths (/apps and
/libs). When scripts are organised in folders which
follow the search path structure, the Mojo will generate two
resource types for each resource type folder. For example:

```text
    src/main/scripts/apps/org/apache/sling/example/example.html
```

will generate the following two resource types

```text
    org/apache/sling/example
    /apps/org/apache/sling/example
```

However, the following script

```text
    src/main/scripts/org/apache/sling/example/example.html
```

will generate only one resource type

```text
    org/apache/sling/example
```

- **Type**: java.util.Set
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No
- **User Property**: scriptingbundle.searchPaths

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--a.3CsourceDirectories.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-metadata-mojo--sourceDirectories"></a><sourceDirectories>**

Defines where this goal will look for scripts in the project. By
default the src/main/scripts and
src/main/resources/javax.script folders will be
considered.

- **Type**: java.util.Set
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No
- **User Property**: scriptingbundle.sourceDirectories

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-usage"></a>

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – Usage

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-usage--Usage"></a>Usage

The Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin will look for scripts in two project directories:

1. src/main/scripts - this folder will contain scripts that will be pre-compiled
2. src/main/resources/javax.script - this folder will contain scripts that will be embedded as is

The structure in these source directories should then follow the normal way of structuring scripts in an Apache Sling application. For more details, check the [URL to Script Resolution](https://sling.apache.org/documentation/the-sling-engine/url-to-script-resolution.html#script-locations) page. In addition to the normal way of structuring scripts in the file tree, the plugin provides some additional features:

1. Resource Type Versioning  
    This works by putting the scripts in a folder that follows this simple naming convention: <resourceType>/<version>/. The <version> should be a valid semantic version (e.g. 1.0.0)
2. Defining explicit extends relationships (similar to the sling:resourceSuperType property)  
    An extends file in the resource type folder (versioned or not) allows defining this explicit relationship. This file must contain a single line with the resourceType used for the extends capability attribute followed by a ;version=<version-range>; in this case, the plugin will set the extends attribute to the given resourceType and generate a Require-Capability for that resourceType with the given version range.
3. Defining an explicit requirement, without an inheritance relationship (e.g. delegation to another resource type)  
    A requires file (assuming the same conventions and syntax as for the extends file) will generate a Require-Capability for each line based on the given resourceType and version range.
4. The Resource Type can have the form of a path or of a Java package name (e.g. com.mydomain.components.image). When the resource type is defined as a package name, the resource type label will be the last subpackage (i.e. for com.mydomain.components.image, the resource type label will be image).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-usage--Defining_scripts"></a>Defining scripts

As an example, let’s assume the following layout:

```text
src/main/resources/javax.script/
    org.foo/1.0.0
        foo.POST.html
```

This will generate following Provide-Capability:

```text
sling.servlet;
    sling.servlet.resourceTypes:List<String>="org.foo";
    sling.servlet.methods:List<String>=POST;
    version:Version="1.0.0"
```

For more complex examples head over to [https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-0-usage--So_how_do_I_use_the_plugin.3F"></a>So how do I use the plugin?

The plugin doesn’t currently integrate with the maven-bundle-plugin, nor the bnd-maven-plugin. However, the generated Require-Capability and Provide-Capability headers values are simply made available via properties:

```text
${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
```

That makes it reasonable straightforward to use the plugin by just adding it into your build in the prepare-package phase and use the two properties in the manifest writing instructions of another plugin like the maven-bundle-plugin:

```xml
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
    <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>0.2.0</version>
    <executions>
        <execution>
            <phase>prepare-package</phase>
            <goals>
                <goal>metadata</goal>
            </goals>
        </execution>
    </executions>
</plugin>
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.felix</groupId>
    <artifactId>maven-bundle-plugin</artifactId>
    <extensions>true</extensions>
    <configuration>
        <instructions>
            <Provide-Capability>
                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability}
            </Provide-Capability>
            <Require-Capability>
                osgi.extender;filter:="(&amp;(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))",
                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
            </Require-Capability>
        </instructions>
    </configuration>
</plugin>
```
