<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo"></a>

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – scriptingbundle:metadata

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--scriptingbundle:metadata"></a>scriptingbundle:metadata

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:scriptingbundle-maven-plugin:0.2.2:metadata

**Description**:

The metadata goal will generate two Maven project
properties, namely
org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability
and
org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability
which can be used to generate the corresponding OSGi bundle headers
for bundles providing scripts executable by a
ScriptEngine.

**Attributes**:

- Requires a Maven project to be executed.
- Binds by default to the [lifecycle phase](http://maven.apache.org/ref/current/maven-core/lifecycles.html): prepare-package.

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--Optional_Parameters"></a>Optional Parameters

| Name | Type | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <excludes> | String[] | 0.2.0 | Allows defining a list of excluded files and folders or patterns to filter which files should be excluded in the analysis for generating capabilities.The following list provides the default excluded files and patterns:Miscellaneous typical temporary files**/*~, **/#*#, **/.#*, **/%*%, **/._*CVS**/CVS, **/CVS/**, **/.cvsignoreSubversion**/.svn, **/.svn/**Bazaar**/.bzr, **/.bzr/**Mac**/.DS_StoreMercurial**/.hg, **/.hg/**git**/.git, **/.git/**User property is:scriptingbundle.excludes. |
| <includes> | String[] | 0.2.0 | Allows defining a list of included files and folders or patterns to filter which files should be included in the analysis for generating capabilities. By default all files are included.Default value is:**.User property is:scriptingbundle.includes. |
| <scriptEngineMappings> | Map | 0.2.0 | Allows overriding the default extension to script engine mapping, in order to correctly generate thesling.resourceType;scriptEngineProvide-Capabilityattribute value. When configuring this mapping, please make sure to use the script extension as the key and one of the Script Engine's name (obtained fromScriptEngineFactory.getNames()) as the value.The following list represents the default extension to Script Engine mapping:ftlfreemarkergstgstringhtmlhtljavajavaesp, ecmarhinojsp, jspf, jspxjsp |
| <searchPaths> | Set | 0.2.0 | Allows overriding the default search paths (/appsand/libs). When scripts are organised in folders which follow the search path structure, the Mojo will generate two resource types for each resource type folder. For example:src/main/scripts/apps/org/apache/sling/example/example.htmlwill generate the following two resource typesorg/apache/sling/example     /apps/org/apache/sling/exampleHowever, the following scriptsrc/main/scripts/org/apache/sling/example/example.htmlwill generate only one resource typeorg/apache/sling/exampleUser property is:scriptingbundle.searchPaths. |
| <sourceDirectories> | Set | 0.2.0 | Defines where this goal will look for scripts in the project. By default thesrc/main/scriptsandsrc/main/resources/javax.scriptfolders will be considered.User property is:scriptingbundle.sourceDirectories. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--Parameter_Details"></a>Parameter Details

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--a.3Cexcludes.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--excludes"></a><excludes>**

Allows defining a list of excluded files and folders or patterns to
filter which files should be excluded in the analysis for
generating capabilities.

The following list provides the default excluded files and
patterns:

- Miscellaneous typical temporary files\*\*/\*~, \*\*/#\*#, \*\*/.#\*, \*\*/%\*%, \*\*/.\_\*
- CVS\*\*/CVS, \*\*/CVS/\*\*, \*\*/.cvsignore
- Subversion\*\*/.svn, \*\*/.svn/\*\*
- Bazaar\*\*/.bzr, \*\*/.bzr/\*\*
- Mac\*\*/.DS\_Store
- Mercurial\*\*/.hg, \*\*/.hg/\*\*
- git\*\*/.git, \*\*/.git/\*\*

- **Type**: java.lang.String[]
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No
- **User Property**: scriptingbundle.excludes

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--a.3Cincludes.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--includes"></a><includes>**

Allows defining a list of included files and folders or patterns to
filter which files should be included in the analysis for
generating capabilities. By default all files are included.

- **Type**: java.lang.String[]
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No
- **User Property**: scriptingbundle.includes
- **Default**: \*\*

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--a.3CscriptEngineMappings.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--scriptEngineMappings"></a><scriptEngineMappings>**

Allows overriding the default extension to script engine mapping,
in order to correctly generate the
sling.resourceType;scriptEngine
Provide-Capability attribute value. When configuring
this mapping, please make sure to use the script extension as the
key and one of the Script Engine's name (obtained from
ScriptEngineFactory.getNames()) as the value.

The following list represents the default extension to Script
Engine mapping:

- ftlfreemarker
- gstgstring
- htmlhtl
- javajava
- esp, ecmarhino
- jsp, jspf, jspxjsp

- **Type**: java.util.Map
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--a.3CsearchPaths.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--searchPaths"></a><searchPaths>**

Allows overriding the default search paths (/apps and
/libs). When scripts are organised in folders which
follow the search path structure, the Mojo will generate two
resource types for each resource type folder. For example:

```text
    src/main/scripts/apps/org/apache/sling/example/example.html
```

will generate the following two resource types

```text
    org/apache/sling/example
    /apps/org/apache/sling/example
```

However, the following script

```text
    src/main/scripts/org/apache/sling/example/example.html
```

will generate only one resource type

```text
    org/apache/sling/example
```

- **Type**: java.util.Set
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No
- **User Property**: scriptingbundle.searchPaths

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--a.3CsourceDirectories.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-metadata-mojo--sourceDirectories"></a><sourceDirectories>**

Defines where this goal will look for scripts in the project. By
default the src/main/scripts and
src/main/resources/javax.script folders will be
considered.

- **Type**: java.util.Set
- **Since**: 0.2.0
- **Required**: No
- **User Property**: scriptingbundle.sourceDirectories

---

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| scriptingbundle:help | Display help information on scriptingbundle-maven-plugin.Callmvn scriptingbundle:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| scriptingbundle:metadata | Themetadatagoal will generate two Maven project properties, namelyorg.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capabilityandorg.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capabilitywhich can be used to generate the corresponding OSGi bundle headers for bundles providing scripts executable by aScriptEngine. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 8 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>  ...  <build>    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->    <pluginManagement>      <plugins>        <plugin>          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>          <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>          <version>0.2.2</version>        </plugin>        ...      </plugins>    </pluginManagement>    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->    <plugins>      <plugin>        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>        <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>        <version>0.2.2</version>      </plugin>      ...    </plugins>  </build>  ...</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-usage"></a>

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – Usage

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-usage--Usage"></a>Usage

The Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin will look for scripts in two project directories:

1. src/main/scripts - this folder will contain scripts that will be pre-compiled
2. src/main/resources/javax.script - this folder will contain scripts that will be embedded as is

The structure in these source directories should then follow the normal way of structuring scripts in an Apache Sling application. For more details, check the [URL to Script Resolution](https://sling.apache.org/documentation/the-sling-engine/url-to-script-resolution.html#script-locations) page. In addition to the normal way of structuring scripts in the file tree, the plugin provides some additional features:

1. Resource Type Versioning  
    This works by putting the scripts in a folder that follows this simple naming convention: <resourceType>/<version>/. The <version> should be a valid semantic version (e.g. 1.0.0)
2. Defining explicit extends relationships (similar to the sling:resourceSuperType property)  
    An extends file in the resource type folder (versioned or not) allows defining this explicit relationship. This file must contain a single line with the resourceType used for the extends capability attribute followed by a ;version=<version-range>; in this case, the plugin will set the extends attribute to the given resourceType and generate a Require-Capability for that resourceType with the given version range.
3. Defining an explicit requirement, without an inheritance relationship (e.g. delegation to another resource type)  
    A requires file (assuming the same conventions and syntax as for the extends file) will generate a Require-Capability for each line based on the given resourceType and version range.
4. The Resource Type can have the form of a path or of a Java package name (e.g. com.mydomain.components.image). When the resource type is defined as a package name, the resource type label will be the last subpackage (i.e. for com.mydomain.components.image, the resource type label will be image).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-usage--Defining_scripts"></a>Defining scripts

As an example, let’s assume the following layout:

```text
src/main/resources/javax.script/
    org.foo/1.0.0
        foo.POST.html
```

This will generate following Provide-Capability:

```text
sling.servlet;
    sling.servlet.resourceTypes:List<String>="org.foo";
    sling.servlet.methods:List<String>=POST;
    version:Version="1.0.0"
```

For more complex examples head over to [https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-2-2-usage--So_how_do_I_use_the_plugin.3F"></a>So how do I use the plugin?

The plugin doesn’t currently integrate with the maven-bundle-plugin, nor the bnd-maven-plugin. However, the generated Require-Capability and Provide-Capability headers values are simply made available via properties:

```text
${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
```

That makes it reasonable straightforward to use the plugin by just adding it into your build in the prepare-package phase and use the two properties in the manifest writing instructions of another plugin like the maven-bundle-plugin:

```xml
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
    <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>0.2.2</version>
    <executions>
        <execution>
            <phase>prepare-package</phase>
            <goals>
                <goal>metadata</goal>
            </goals>
        </execution>
    </executions>
</plugin>
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.felix</groupId>
    <artifactId>maven-bundle-plugin</artifactId>
    <extensions>true</extensions>
    <configuration>
        <instructions>
            <Provide-Capability>
                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability}
            </Provide-Capability>
            <Require-Capability>
                osgi.extender;filter:="(&amp;(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))",
                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
            </Require-Capability>
        </instructions>
    </configuration>
</plugin>
```

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| scriptingbundle:help | Display help information on scriptingbundle-maven-plugin.Callmvn scriptingbundle:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| scriptingbundle:metadata | Themetadatagoal will generate two Maven project properties, namelyorg.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capabilityandorg.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capabilitywhich can be used to generate the corresponding OSGi bundle headers for bundles providing scripts executable by aScriptEngine. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

| Maven | 2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 8 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>  ...  <build>    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->    <pluginManagement>      <plugins>        <plugin>          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>          <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>          <version>0.3.0</version>        </plugin>        ...      </plugins>    </pluginManagement>    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->    <plugins>      <plugin>        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>        <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>        <version>0.3.0</version>      </plugin>      ...    </plugins>  </build>  ...</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-usage"></a>

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – Usage

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-usage--Usage"></a>Usage

The plugin can be used either as a regular Maven plugin or as a BND plugin.

No matter which approach you choose, the plugin will by default look for scripts in two project directories:

1. src/main/scripts - this folder will contain scripts that will be pre-compiled
2. src/main/resources/javax.script - this folder will contain scripts that will be embedded as is

The structure in these source directories should then follow the normal way of structuring scripts in an Apache Sling application. For more details, check the [URL to Script Resolution](https://sling.apache.org/documentation/the-sling-engine/url-to-script-resolution.html#script-locations) page. In addition to the normal way of structuring scripts in the file tree, the plugin provides some additional features:

1. Resource Type Versioning  
    This works by putting the scripts in a folder that follows this simple naming convention: <resourceType>/<version>/. The <version> should be a valid semantic version (e.g. 1.0.0)
2. Defining explicit extends relationships (similar to the sling:resourceSuperType property)  
    An extends file in the resource type folder (versioned or not) allows defining this explicit relationship. This file must contain a single line with the resourceType used for the extends capability attribute followed by a ;version=<version-range>; in this case, the plugin will set the extends attribute to the given resourceType and generate a Require-Capability for that resourceType with the given version range.
3. Defining an explicit requirement, without an inheritance relationship (e.g. delegation to another resource type)  
    A requires file (assuming the same conventions and syntax as for the extends file) will generate a Require-Capability for each line based on the given resourceType and version range.
4. The Resource Type can have the form of a path or of a Java package name (e.g. com.mydomain.components.image). When the resource type is defined as a package name, the resource type label will be the last subpackage (i.e. for com.mydomain.components.image, the resource type label will be image).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-usage--Defining_scripts"></a>Defining scripts

As an example, let’s assume the following layout:

```text
src/main/resources/javax.script/
    org.foo/1.0.0
        foo.POST.html
```

This will generate following Provide-Capability:

```text
sling.servlet;
    sling.servlet.resourceTypes:List<String>="org.foo";
    sling.servlet.methods:List<String>=POST;
    version:Version="1.0.0"
```

For more complex examples head over to [https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-usage--So_how_do_I_use_the_plugin.3F"></a>So how do I use the plugin?

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-usage--Maven_Plugin"></a>Maven Plugin

When used as a Maven plugin, the generated Require-Capability and Provide-Capability headers values are made available via properties:

```text
${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
```

That makes it reasonably straightforward to use the plugin by just adding it into your build and use the two properties in the manifest writing instructions of another plugin like the maven-bundle-plugin:

```xml
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
    <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>0.3.0</version>
    <executions>
        <execution>
            <phase>prepare-package</phase>
            <goals>
                <goal>metadata</goal>
            </goals>
        </execution>
    </executions>
</plugin>
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.felix</groupId>
    <artifactId>maven-bundle-plugin</artifactId>
    <extensions>true</extensions>
    <configuration>
        <instructions>
            <Provide-Capability>
                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability}
            </Provide-Capability>
            <Require-Capability>
                osgi.extender;filter:="(&amp;(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))",
                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
            </Require-Capability>
        </instructions>
    </configuration>
</plugin>
```

The osgi.extender requirement is mandatory to have the bundle wired up to the Apache Sling Servlets Resolver, but this should be manually defined by the developers, so that their bundle is correctly wired up to whatever version of the Servlets Resolver is available on the destination platform.

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-3-0-usage--BND_Plugin"></a>BND Plugin

Starting with version 0.3.0, the JAR also provides a BND plugin. The simplest configuration (where the defaults are used) would look like:

```xml
<plugin>
    <groupId>biz.aQute.bnd</groupId>
    <artifactId>bnd-maven-plugin</artifactId>
    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
            <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>0.3.0</version>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
</plugin>
```

and the following instructions added to your project’s bnd.bnd file:

```text
Require-Capability:             osgi.extender;filter:="(&(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))"
-plugin:                        org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.plugin.bnd.BundledScriptsScannerPlugin
```

The BND plugin supports the same configuration options as the Maven metadata goal, using the exact same name for its configuration properties. Multiple values need to be provided as a quoted comma separated values list (e.g. sourceDirectories="src/main/scripts,src/main/resources/javax.script", scriptEngineMappings="html:htl,js:rhino").

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-bnd"></a>

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin –

Starting with version `0.3.0`, the JAR also provides a [bnd plugin](https://bnd.bndtools.org/chapters/870-plugins.html). The simplest configuration (where the defaults are used) would look like:

```xml
<plugin>    <groupId>biz.aQute.bnd</groupId>    <artifactId>bnd-maven-plugin</artifactId>    <dependencies>        <dependency>            <groupId>${project.groupId}</groupId>            <artifactId>${project.artifactId}</artifactId>            <version>${project.version}</version>        </dependency>    </dependencies></plugin>
```

and the following instructions added to your project’s `bnd.bnd` file:

```text
Require-Capability:             osgi.extender;filter:="(&(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))"-plugin:                        org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.plugin.bnd.BundledScriptsScannerPlugin
```

The bnd plugin supports the same configuration options as the [Maven `metadata` goal](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-metadata-mojo), using the exact same name for its configuration properties. Multiple values need to be provided as a quoted comma-separated values list (e.g. `sourceDirectories="src/main/scripts,src/main/resources/javax.script"`, `scriptEngineMappings="html:htl,js:rhino"`).

For a general usage description please refer to [Usage](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-usage).

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-index"></a>

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin –

The Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin helps with generating the OSGi bundle capability headers that bundles which provide embedded or precompiled scripts for server-side rendering in an Apache Sling application require in order to have themselves wired up to the Apache Sling Servlets Resolver. Details on the necessary headers are described at [Bundled Scripts](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-scripting--bundled-scripts). When executed, the plugin will define two project properties (`org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability` and `org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability`) which can be used to populate the corresponding bundle headers.

Bundles that get extended by the [`org.apache.sling.servlets.resolver`](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-servlets-resolver) with these `Requirements` and `Capabilities` will have their scripts made available automatically with added versioning and dependency support.

Manually defining the `Require-Capability` and `Provide-Capability` bundle headers is error-prone and unnecessary, as they can be derived from the file-system layout required for scripts by the resolver (for the most part).

Starting with version `0.3.0`, the JAR also provides a [bnd plugin](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-bnd).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-index--Usage"></a>Usage

General instructions on how to use the Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin can be found on the [usage](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-usage) page.

In case you still have questions regarding the plugin’s usage feel free to contact the Apache Sling Development List. The posts to the mailing list are archived and could already contain the answer to your question as part of an older thread. Hence, it is also worth browsing/searching the mail archive.

If you feel like the plugin is missing a feature or has a defect, you can fill a feature request or bug report in our issue tracker. When creating a new issue, please provide a comprehensive description of your concern. Especially for fixing bugs it is crucial that the developers can reproduce your problem. For this reason, entire debug logs, POMs or most preferably little demo projects attached to the issue are very much appreciated. Of course, patches are welcome, too. Contributors can check out the project from our source repository and will find supplementary information in the Maven guide.

```xml
<project>  ...  <build>    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->    <pluginManagement>      <plugins>        <plugin>          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>          <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>          <version>0.4.0</version>        </plugin>        ...      </plugins>    </pluginManagement>    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->    <plugins>      <plugin>        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>        <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>        <version>0.4.0</version>      </plugin>      ...    </plugins>  </build>  ...</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-usage"></a>

# Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – Usage

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-usage--Usage"></a>Usage

The plugin can be used either as a regular Maven plugin or as a [bnd plugin](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-bnd).

No matter which approach you choose, the plugin will by default look for scripts in two project directories:

1. `src/main/scripts` - this folder will contain scripts that will be pre-compiled
2. `src/main/resources/javax.script` - this folder will contain scripts that will be embedded as is

The structure in these source directories should then follow the normal way of structuring scripts in an Apache Sling application. For more details, check the [Sling Scripting](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-scripting--resource-script-naming-conventions) page. In addition to the normal way of structuring scripts in the file tree, the plugin provides some additional features:

1. Resource Type Versioning  
    This works by putting the scripts in a folder that follows this simple naming convention: `<resourceType>/<version>/`. The `<version>` should be a valid semantic version (e.g. `1.0.0`)
2. Defining explicit extends relationships (similar to the `sling:resourceSuperType` property)  
    An `extends` file in the resource type folder (versioned or not) allows defining this explicit relationship. This file must contain a single line with the `resourceType` used for the `extends` capability attribute followed by a `;version=<version-range>`; in this case, the plugin will set the `extends` attribute to the given `resourceType` and generate a `Require-Capability` for that `resourceType` with the given version range. To generate an optional capability header (when the bundled script extends from a non-bundle, resource script), append `;resolution:=optional` to the line. The line must comply with the OSGI common header syntax from [OSGI Core R7 §3.2.4](http://docs.osgi.org/specification/osgi.core/7.0.0/framework.module.html#framework.common.header.syntax).
3. Defining an explicit requirement, without an inheritance relationship (e.g. delegation to another resource type)  
    A `requires` file (assuming the same conventions and syntax as for the `extends` file) will generate a `Require-Capability` for each line based on the given `resourceType` and version range.
4. The Resource Type can have the form of a path or of a Java package name (e.g. `com.mydomain.components.image`). When the resource type is defined as a package name, the resource type label will be the last subpackage (i.e. for `com.mydomain.components.image`, the resource type label will be `image`).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-usage--Defining_scripts"></a>Defining scripts

As an example, let’s assume the following layout:

```text
src/main/resources/javax.script/    org.foo/1.0.0        foo.POST.html
```

This will generate following `Provide-Capability`:

```text
sling.servlet;    sling.servlet.resourceTypes:List<String>="org.foo";    sling.servlet.methods:List<String>=POST;    version:Version="1.0.0"
```

For more complex examples head over to [https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-4-0-usage--Configure_Maven_Plugin"></a>Configure Maven Plugin

When used as a Maven plugin, the generated `Require-Capability` and `Provide-Capability` headers values are made available via Maven project properties:

```text
${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
```

That makes it reasonably straightforward to use the plugin by just adding it into your build and use the two properties in the manifest writing instructions of another plugin like the `maven-bundle-plugin`:

```xml
<plugin>    <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>    <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>    <version>0.4.0</version>    <executions>        <execution>            <phase>prepare-package</phase>            <goals>                <goal>metadata</goal>            </goals>        </execution>    </executions></plugin><plugin>    <groupId>org.apache.felix</groupId>    <artifactId>maven-bundle-plugin</artifactId>    <extensions>true</extensions>    <configuration>        <instructions>            <Provide-Capability>                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability}            </Provide-Capability>            <Require-Capability>                osgi.extender;filter:="(&amp;(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))",                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}            </Require-Capability>        </instructions>    </configuration></plugin>
```

The `osgi.extender` requirement is mandatory to have the bundle wired up to the Apache Sling Servlets Resolver, but this should be manually defined by the developers, so that their bundle is correctly wired up to whatever version of the Servlets Resolver is available on the destination platform.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-bnd"></a>

# Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – bnd Plugin

# bnd Plugin

Starting with version `0.3.0`, the JAR also provides a [bnd plugin](https://bnd.bndtools.org/chapters/870-plugins.html). The simplest configuration (where the defaults are used) would look like:

```xml
<plugin>    <groupId>biz.aQute.bnd</groupId>    <artifactId>bnd-maven-plugin</artifactId>    <dependencies>        <dependency>            <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>            <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>            <version>0.5.0</version>        </dependency>    </dependencies></plugin>
```

and the following instructions added to your project’s `bnd.bnd` file:

```text
Require-Capability:             osgi.extender;filter:="(&(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))"-plugin:                        org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.plugin.bnd.BundledScriptsScannerPlugin
```

The bnd plugin supports the same configuration options as the [Maven `metadata` goal](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-metadata-mojo), using the exact same name for its configuration properties. Multiple values need to be provided as a quoted comma-separated values list (e.g. `sourceDirectories="src/main/scripts,src/main/resources/javax.script"`, `scriptEngineMappings="html:htl,js:rhino"`).

For a general usage description please refer to [Usage](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-usage).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-bnd--Working_with_FileVault_content_package_projects"></a>Working with [FileVault](https://jackrabbit.apache.org/filevault/index.html) content package projects

Starting with version 0.5.0, the bnd plugin can be used to scan [FileVault](https://jackrabbit.apache.org/filevault/index.html) content package projects. The same concepts from the [generic usage](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-usage) instructions apply, with two differences:

1. Since content packages contain the serialisation of resource properties, the Docview `.content.xml` files will be parsed and the encountered `sling:resourceSuperType` properties will be directly used to generate the appropriate OSGi capabilities, making the `extends` file redundant (besides, the `extends` files should not be packed in a content package anyways).
2. When delegating to another resource type, you can define this relationship in your component’s Docview `.content.xml` file, by using a new multi-value String property - `sling:requiredResourceTypes`. This property is only used by the bnd plugin to generate the correct `Require-Capability` header values. An example is available [here](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/blob/master/examples/org-apache-sling-scripting-content-package-with-bundle-attached/src/main/content/jcr_root/apps/sling/scripting/example-cp/hello/.content.xml). When using the `sling:requiredResourceTypes` Docview property, the `requires` file is redundant.

A trivial example of the bnd plugin configured to extract capabilities from a content package, together with the required plugins to also generate a `jar` file with the precompiled scripts can be seen [here](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/blob/master/examples/org-apache-sling-scripting-content-package-with-bundle-attached/pom.xml).

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-index"></a>

# Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin –

The Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin helps with generating the OSGi bundle capability headers that bundles which provide embedded or precompiled scripts for server-side rendering in an Apache Sling application require in order to have themselves wired up to the Apache Sling Servlets Resolver. Details on the necessary headers are described at [Bundled Scripts](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-scripting--bundled-scripts). When executed, the plugin will define two project properties (`org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability` and `org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability`) which can be used to populate the corresponding bundle headers.

Bundles that get extended by the [`org.apache.sling.servlets.resolver`](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-servlets-resolver) with these `Requirements` and `Capabilities` will have their scripts made available automatically with added versioning and dependency support.

Manually defining the `Require-Capability` and `Provide-Capability` bundle headers is error-prone and unnecessary, as they can be derived from the file-system layout required for scripts by the resolver (for the most part).

Starting with version `0.3.0`, the JAR also provides a [bnd plugin](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-bnd).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-index--Usage"></a>Usage

General instructions on how to use the Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin can be found on the [usage](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-usage) page.

In case you still have questions regarding the plugin’s usage feel free to contact the Apache Sling Development List. The posts to the mailing list are archived and could already contain the answer to your question as part of an older thread. Hence, it is also worth browsing/searching the mail archive.

If you feel like the plugin is missing a feature or has a defect, you can fill a feature request or bug report in our issue tracker. When creating a new issue, please provide a comprehensive description of your concern. Especially for fixing bugs it is crucial that the developers can reproduce your problem. For this reason, entire debug logs, POMs or most preferably little demo projects attached to the issue are very much appreciated. Of course, patches are welcome, too. Contributors can check out the project from our source repository and will find supplementary information in the Maven guide.

# Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| scriptingbundle:help | Display help information on scriptingbundle-maven-plugin.Callmvn scriptingbundle:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| scriptingbundle:metadata | Themetadatagoal will generate two Maven project properties, namelyorg.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capabilityandorg.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capabilitywhich can be used to generate the corresponding OSGi bundle headers for bundles providing scripts executable by aScriptEngine. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.6.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.7 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>  ...  <build>    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->    <pluginManagement>      <plugins>        <plugin>          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>          <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>          <version>0.5.0</version>        </plugin>        ...      </plugins>    </pluginManagement>    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->    <plugins>      <plugin>        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>        <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>        <version>0.5.0</version>      </plugin>      ...    </plugins>  </build>  ...</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-usage"></a>

# Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – Usage

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-usage--Usage"></a>Usage

The plugin can be used either as a regular Maven plugin or as a [bnd plugin](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-bnd). Its purpose is to extract the capabilities required for packaging the scripts (precompiled or not) into an OSGi bundle. Both versions of the plugin can be used for OSGi bundle projects, however the [bnd plugin](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-bnd) can also be used with [FileVault](https://jackrabbit.apache.org/filevault/index.html) content package projects.

Both versions of the plugin will, by default, look for scripts in two project directories:

1. `src/main/scripts` - this folder will contain scripts that will be pre-compiled
2. `src/main/resources/javax.script` - this folder will contain scripts that will be embedded as is

The structure in these source directories should then follow the normal way of structuring scripts in an Apache Sling application. For more details, check the [Sling Scripting](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-scripting--resource-script-naming-conventions) page. In addition to the normal way of structuring scripts in the file tree, the plugin provides some additional features:

1. Resource Type Versioning  
    This works by putting the scripts in a folder that follows this simple naming convention: `<resourceType>/<version>/`. The `<version>` should be a valid semantic version (e.g. `1.0.0`)
2. Defining explicit extends relationships (similar to the `sling:resourceSuperType` property)  
    An `extends` file in the resource type folder (versioned or not) allows defining this explicit relationship. This file must contain a single line with the `resourceType` used for the `extends` capability attribute followed by a `;version=<version-range>`; in this case, the plugin will set the `extends` attribute to the given `resourceType` and generate a `Require-Capability` for that `resourceType` with the given version range. To generate an optional capability header (when the bundled script extends from a non-bundle, resource script), append `;resolution:=optional` to the line. The line must comply with the OSGI common header syntax from [OSGI Core R7 §3.2.4](http://docs.osgi.org/specification/osgi.core/7.0.0/framework.module.html#framework.common.header.syntax).
3. Defining an explicit requirement, without an inheritance relationship (e.g. delegation to another resource type)  
    A `requires` file (assuming the same conventions and syntax as for the `extends` file) will generate a `Require-Capability` for each line based on the given `resourceType` and version range.
4. The Resource Type can have the form of a path or of a Java package name (e.g. `com.mydomain.components.image`). When the resource type is defined as a package name, the resource type label will be the last subpackage (i.e. for `com.mydomain.components.image`, the resource type label will be `image`).

Starting with version 0.5.0, the plugin will mark the requirements which are not satisfied by the analysed project as optional; classpath dependencies are not checked for provided capabilities. If you want to generate mandatory requirements, set the `missingRequirementsOptional` flag to `false`.

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-usage--Defining_scripts"></a>Defining scripts

As an example, let’s assume the following layout:

```text
src/main/resources/javax.script/    org.foo/1.0.0        foo.POST.html
```

This will generate following `Provide-Capability`:

```text
sling.servlet;    sling.servlet.resourceTypes:List<String>="org.foo";    sling.servlet.methods:List<String>=POST;    version:Version="1.0.0"
```

For more complex examples head over to [https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-0-usage--Configure_Maven_Plugin"></a>Configure Maven Plugin

When used as a Maven plugin, the generated `Require-Capability` and `Provide-Capability` headers values are made available via Maven project properties:

```text
${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
```

That makes it reasonably straightforward to use the plugin by just adding it into your build and use the two properties in the manifest writing instructions of another plugin like the `maven-bundle-plugin`:

```xml
<plugin>    <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>    <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>    <version>0.5.0</version>    <executions>        <execution>            <phase>prepare-package</phase>            <goals>                <goal>metadata</goal>            </goals>        </execution>    </executions></plugin><plugin>    <groupId>org.apache.felix</groupId>    <artifactId>maven-bundle-plugin</artifactId>    <extensions>true</extensions>    <configuration>        <instructions>            <Provide-Capability>                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability}            </Provide-Capability>            <Require-Capability>                osgi.extender;filter:="(&amp;(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))",                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}            </Require-Capability>        </instructions>    </configuration></plugin>
```

The `osgi.extender` requirement is mandatory to have the bundle wired up to the Apache Sling Servlets Resolver, but this should be manually defined by the developers, so that their bundle is correctly wired up to whatever version of the Servlets Resolver is available on the destination platform.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-bnd"></a>

# Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – bnd Plugin

# bnd Plugin

Starting with version `0.3.0`, the JAR also provides a [bnd plugin](https://bnd.bndtools.org/chapters/870-plugins.html). The simplest configuration (where the defaults are used) would look like:

```xml
<plugin>    <groupId>biz.aQute.bnd</groupId>    <artifactId>bnd-maven-plugin</artifactId>    <dependencies>        <dependency>            <groupId>${project.groupId}</groupId>            <artifactId>${project.artifactId}</artifactId>            <version>${project.version}</version>        </dependency>    </dependencies></plugin>
```

and the following instructions added to your project’s `bnd.bnd` file:

```text
Require-Capability:             osgi.extender;filter:="(&(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))"-plugin:                        org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.plugin.bnd.BundledScriptsScannerPlugin
```

The bnd plugin supports the same configuration options as the [Maven `metadata` goal](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-metadata-mojo), using the exact same name for its configuration properties. Multiple values need to be provided as a quoted comma-separated values list (e.g. `sourceDirectories="src/main/scripts,src/main/resources/javax.script"`, `scriptEngineMappings="html:htl,js:rhino"`).

For a general usage description please refer to [Usage](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-usage).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-bnd--Working_with_FileVault_content_package_projects"></a>Working with [FileVault](https://jackrabbit.apache.org/filevault/index.html) content package projects

Starting with version 0.5.0, the bnd plugin can be used to scan [FileVault](https://jackrabbit.apache.org/filevault/index.html) content package projects. The same concepts from the [generic usage](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-usage) instructions apply, with two differences:

1. Since content packages contain the serialisation of resource properties, the Docview `.content.xml` files will be parsed and the encountered `sling:resourceSuperType` properties will be directly used to generate the appropriate OSGi capabilities, making the `extends` file redundant (besides, the `extends` files should not be packed in a content package anyways).
2. When delegating to another resource type, you can define this relationship in your component’s Docview `.content.xml` file, by using a new multi-value String property - `sling:requiredResourceTypes`. This property is only used by the bnd plugin to generate the correct `Require-Capability` header values. An example is available [here](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/blob/master/examples/org-apache-sling-scripting-content-package-with-bundle-attached/src/main/content/jcr_root/apps/sling/scripting/example-cp/hello/.content.xml). When using the `sling:requiredResourceTypes` Docview property, the `requires` file is redundant.

A trivial example of the bnd plugin configured to extract capabilities from a content package, together with the required plugins to also generate a `jar` file with the precompiled scripts can be seen [here](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/blob/master/examples/org-apache-sling-scripting-content-package-with-bundle-attached/pom.xml).

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-index"></a>

# Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin –

The Apache Sling Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin helps with generating the OSGi bundle capability headers that bundles which provide embedded or precompiled scripts for server-side rendering in an Apache Sling application require in order to have themselves wired up to the Apache Sling Servlets Resolver. Details on the necessary headers are described at [Bundled Scripts](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-scripting--bundled-scripts). When executed, the plugin will define two project properties (`org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability` and `org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability`) which can be used to populate the corresponding bundle headers.

Bundles that get extended by the [`org.apache.sling.servlets.resolver`](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-servlets-resolver) with these `Requirements` and `Capabilities` will have their scripts made available automatically with added versioning and dependency support.

Manually defining the `Require-Capability` and `Provide-Capability` bundle headers is error-prone and unnecessary, as they can be derived from the file-system layout required for scripts by the resolver (for the most part).

Starting with version `0.3.0`, the JAR also provides a [bnd plugin](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-bnd).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-index--Usage"></a>Usage

General instructions on how to use the Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin can be found on the [usage](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-usage) page.

In case you still have questions regarding the plugin’s usage feel free to contact the Apache Sling Development List. The posts to the mailing list are archived and could already contain the answer to your question as part of an older thread. Hence, it is also worth browsing/searching the mail archive.

If you feel like the plugin is missing a feature or has a defect, you can fill a feature request or bug report in our issue tracker. When creating a new issue, please provide a comprehensive description of your concern. Especially for fixing bugs it is crucial that the developers can reproduce your problem. For this reason, entire debug logs, POMs or most preferably little demo projects attached to the issue are very much appreciated. Of course, patches are welcome, too. Contributors can check out the project from our source repository and will find supplementary information in the Maven guide.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-usage"></a>

# Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – Usage

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-usage--Usage"></a>Usage

The plugin can be used either as a regular Maven plugin or as a [bnd plugin](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-bnd). Its purpose is to extract the capabilities required for packaging the scripts (precompiled or not) into an OSGi bundle. Both versions of the plugin can be used for OSGi bundle projects, however the [bnd plugin](#sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-bnd) can also be used with [FileVault](https://jackrabbit.apache.org/filevault/index.html) content package projects.

Both versions of the plugin will, by default, look for scripts in two project directories:

1. `src/main/scripts` - this folder will contain scripts that will be pre-compiled
2. `src/main/resources/javax.script` - this folder will contain scripts that will be embedded as is

The structure in these source directories should then follow the normal way of structuring scripts in an Apache Sling application. For more details, check the [Sling Scripting](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-scripting--resource-script-naming-conventions) page. In addition to the normal way of structuring scripts in the file tree, the plugin provides some additional features:

1. Resource Type Versioning  
    This works by putting the scripts in a folder that follows this simple naming convention: `<resourceType>/<version>/`. The `<version>` should be a valid semantic version (e.g. `1.0.0`)
2. Defining explicit extends relationships (similar to the `sling:resourceSuperType` property)  
    An `extends` file in the resource type folder (versioned or not) allows defining this explicit relationship. This file must contain a single line with the `resourceType` used for the `extends` capability attribute followed by a `;version=<version-range>`; in this case, the plugin will set the `extends` attribute to the given `resourceType` and generate a `Require-Capability` for that `resourceType` with the given version range. To generate an optional capability header (when the bundled script extends from a non-bundle, resource script), append `;resolution:=optional` to the line. The line must comply with the OSGI common header syntax from [OSGI Core R7 §3.2.4](http://docs.osgi.org/specification/osgi.core/7.0.0/framework.module.html#framework.common.header.syntax).
3. Defining an explicit requirement, without an inheritance relationship (e.g. delegation to another resource type)  
    A `requires` file (assuming the same conventions and syntax as for the `extends` file) will generate a `Require-Capability` for each line based on the given `resourceType` and version range.
4. The Resource Type can have the form of a path or of a Java package name (e.g. `com.mydomain.components.image`). When the resource type is defined as a package name, the resource type label will be the last subpackage (i.e. for `com.mydomain.components.image`, the resource type label will be `image`).

Starting with version 0.5.0, the plugin will mark the requirements which are not satisfied by the analysed project as optional; classpath dependencies are not checked for provided capabilities. If you want to generate mandatory requirements, set the `missingRequirementsOptional` flag to `false`.

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-usage--Defining_scripts"></a>Defining scripts

As an example, let’s assume the following layout:

```text
src/main/resources/javax.script/    org.foo/1.0.0        foo.POST.html
```

This will generate following `Provide-Capability`:

```text
sling.servlet;    sling.servlet.resourceTypes:List<String>="org.foo";    sling.servlet.methods:List<String>=POST;    version:Version="1.0.0"
```

For more complex examples head over to [https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples](https://github.com/apache/sling-org-apache-sling-scripting-bundle-tracker-it/tree/master/examples).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-archives-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-0-5-2-usage--Configure_Maven_Plugin"></a>Configure Maven Plugin

When used as a Maven plugin, the generated `Require-Capability` and `Provide-Capability` headers values are made available via Maven project properties:

```text
${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}
```

That makes it reasonably straightforward to use the plugin by just adding it into your build and use the two properties in the manifest writing instructions of another plugin like the `maven-bundle-plugin`:

```xml
<plugin>    <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>    <artifactId>scriptingbundle-maven-plugin</artifactId>    <version>0.5.2</version>    <executions>        <execution>            <phase>prepare-package</phase>            <goals>                <goal>metadata</goal>            </goals>        </execution>    </executions></plugin><plugin>    <groupId>org.apache.felix</groupId>    <artifactId>maven-bundle-plugin</artifactId>    <extensions>true</extensions>    <configuration>        <instructions>            <Provide-Capability>                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability}            </Provide-Capability>            <Require-Capability>                osgi.extender;filter:="(&amp;(osgi.extender=sling.scripting)(version>=1.0.0)(!(version>=2.0.0)))",                ${org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability}            </Require-Capability>        </instructions>    </configuration></plugin>
```

The `osgi.extender` requirement is mandatory to have the bundle wired up to the Apache Sling Servlets Resolver, but this should be manually defined by the developers, so that their bundle is correctly wired up to whatever version of the Servlets Resolver is available on the destination platform.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo"></a>

# Scripting Bundle Maven Plugin – scriptingbundle:metadata

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--scriptingbundle:metadata"></a>scriptingbundle:metadata

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:scriptingbundle-maven-plugin:0.5.2:metadata

**Description**:

The `metadata` goal will generate two Maven project
properties, namely
`org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Require-Capability`
and
`org.apache.sling.scriptingbundle.maven.plugin.Provide-Capability`
which can be used to generate the corresponding OSGi bundle headers
for bundles providing scripts executable by a
`ScriptEngine`.

**Attributes**:

- Requires a Maven project to be executed.
- Binds by default to the [lifecycle phase](http://maven.apache.org/ref/current/maven-core/lifecycles.html): `prepare-package`.

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--Optional_Parameters"></a>Optional Parameters

| Name | Type | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <excludes> | String[] | 0.2.0 | Allows defining a list of excluded files and folders or patterns to filter which files should be excluded in the analysis for generating capabilities.The following list provides the default excluded files and patterns:Miscellaneous typical temporary files**/*~, **/#*#, **/.#*, **/%*%, **/._*CVS**/CVS, **/CVS/**, **/.cvsignoreSubversion**/.svn, **/.svn/**Bazaar**/.bzr, **/.bzr/**Mac**/.DS_StoreMercurial**/.hg, **/.hg/**git**/.git, **/.git/**User property is:scriptingbundle.excludes. |
| <includes> | String[] | 0.2.0 | Allows defining a list of included files and folders or patterns to filter which files should be included in the analysis for generating capabilities. By default all files are included.Default value is:**.User property is:scriptingbundle.includes. |
| <missingRequirementsOptional> | boolean | 0.5.0 | When set to "true", the requirements which are not satisfied directly by this project will be marked as optional.Default value is:true.User property is:scriptingbundle.missingRequirementsOptional. |
| <scriptEngineMappings> | Map | 0.2.0 | Allows overriding the default extension to script engine mapping, in order to correctly generate thesling.resourceType;scriptEngineProvide-Capabilityattribute value. When configuring this mapping, please make sure to use the script extension as the key and one of the Script Engine's names (obtained fromScriptEngineFactory.getNames()) as the value.The following list represents the default extension to Script Engine mapping:ftlfreemarkergstgstringhtmlhtljavajavaesp, ecmarhinojsp, jspf, jspxjsp |
| <searchPaths> | Set | 0.2.0 | Allows overriding the default search paths (/appsand/libs). When scripts are organised in folders which follow the search path structure, the Mojo will generate two resource types for each resource type folder. For example:src/main/scripts/apps/org/apache/sling/example/example.htmlwill generate the following two resource typesorg/apache/sling/example     /apps/org/apache/sling/exampleHowever, the following scriptsrc/main/scripts/org/apache/sling/example/example.htmlwill generate only one resource typeorg/apache/sling/exampleUser property is:scriptingbundle.searchPaths. |
| <sourceDirectories> | Set | 0.2.0 | Defines where this goal will look for scripts in the project. By default thesrc/main/scriptsandsrc/main/resources/javax.scriptfolders will be considered.User property is:scriptingbundle.sourceDirectories. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--Parameter_Details"></a>Parameter Details

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--a.3Cexcludes.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--excludes"></a><excludes>**

Allows defining a list of excluded files and folders or patterns to
filter which files should be excluded in the analysis for
generating capabilities.

The following list provides the default excluded files and
patterns:

- Miscellaneous typical temporary files\*\*/\*~, \*\*/#\*#, \*\*/.#\*, \*\*/%\*%, \*\*/.\_\*
- CVS\*\*/CVS, \*\*/CVS/\*\*, \*\*/.cvsignore
- Subversion\*\*/.svn, \*\*/.svn/\*\*
- Bazaar\*\*/.bzr, \*\*/.bzr/\*\*
- Mac\*\*/.DS\_Store
- Mercurial\*\*/.hg, \*\*/.hg/\*\*
- git\*\*/.git, \*\*/.git/\*\*

- **Type**: `java.lang.String[]`
- **Since**: `0.2.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `scriptingbundle.excludes`

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--a.3Cincludes.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--includes"></a><includes>**

Allows defining a list of included files and folders or patterns to
filter which files should be included in the analysis for
generating capabilities. By default all files are included.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String[]`
- **Since**: `0.2.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `scriptingbundle.includes`
- **Default**: `**`

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--a.3CmissingRequirementsOptional.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--missingRequirementsOptional"></a><missingRequirementsOptional>**

When set to "true", the requirements which are not satisfied
directly by this project will be marked as optional.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Since**: `0.5.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `scriptingbundle.missingRequirementsOptional`
- **Default**: `true`

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--a.3CscriptEngineMappings.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--scriptEngineMappings"></a><scriptEngineMappings>**

Allows overriding the default extension to script engine mapping,
in order to correctly generate the
`sling.resourceType;scriptEngine`
`Provide-Capability` attribute value. When configuring
this mapping, please make sure to use the script extension as the
key and one of the Script Engine's names (obtained from
`ScriptEngineFactory.getNames()`) as the value.

The following list represents the default extension to Script
Engine mapping:

- ftlfreemarker
- gstgstring
- htmlhtl
- javajava
- esp, ecmarhino
- jsp, jspf, jspxjsp

- **Type**: `java.util.Map`
- **Since**: `0.2.0`
- **Required**: `No`

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--a.3CsearchPaths.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--searchPaths"></a><searchPaths>**

Allows overriding the default search paths (`/apps` and
`/libs`). When scripts are organised in folders which
follow the search path structure, the Mojo will generate two
resource types for each resource type folder. For example:

```text
    src/main/scripts/apps/org/apache/sling/example/example.html
```

will generate the following two resource types

```text
    org/apache/sling/example
    /apps/org/apache/sling/example
```

However, the following script

```text
    src/main/scripts/org/apache/sling/example/example.html
```

will generate only one resource type

```text
    org/apache/sling/example
```

- **Type**: `java.util.Set`
- **Since**: `0.2.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `scriptingbundle.searchPaths`

---

#### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--a.3CsourceDirectories.3E"></a>**<a id="sling-apache-org-components-scriptingbundle-maven-plugin-metadata-mojo--sourceDirectories"></a><sourceDirectories>**

Defines where this goal will look for scripts in the project. By
default the `src/main/scripts` and
`src/main/resources/javax.script` folders will be
considered.

- **Type**: `java.util.Set`
- **Since**: `0.2.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `scriptingbundle.sourceDirectories`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-archives-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-1-0-12-plugin-info"></a>

# Plugin Documentation – Apache Sling Feature Model Converter Plugin

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-archives-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-1-0-12-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

# Plugin Documentation

This report describes goals, parameters details, requirements and sample usage of this plugin.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-archives-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-1-0-12-plugin-info--Goals"></a>

## Goals

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| sling-feature-converter:convert-cp | Converts the given Content Packages into Feature Models and places the converted Content Package into the local Maven Repository |
| sling-feature-converter:convert-pm | Converts the given list of Provisioning Models into Feature Models |
| sling-feature-converter:help | Display help information on sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin.Callmvn sling-feature-converter:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-archives-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-1-0-12-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

## System Requirements

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.8.1 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 11 |

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-archives-sling-feature-converter-maven-plugin-1-0-12-plugin-info--System_Requirements_History"></a>
