<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation"></a>

# Apache Sling Maven Plugin – Bundle Installation/Uninstallation

# Bundle Installation/Uninstallation

There are three different installation approaches supported by the plugin which behave differently for the installation and uninstallation. In the following section all mechanisms are outlined individually for both use cases.

- [Deploy/Upload/Install](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Deploy.2FUpload.2FInstall)
  - [Felix Web Console](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Felix_Web_Console)
  - [WebDAV PUT](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--WebDAV_PUT)
  - [Sling POST Servlet](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Sling_POST_Servlet)
- [Undeploy/Uninstall](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Undeploy.2FUninstall)
  - [Felix Web Console](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Felix_Web_Console)
  - [WebDAV PUT](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--WebDAV_PUT)
  - [Sling POST Servlet](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Sling_POST_Servlet)
- [Intermediate Resources](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Intermediate_Resources)

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Deploy.2FUpload.2FInstall"></a>Deploy/Upload/Install[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--deploy-upload-install)

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Felix_Web_Console"></a>Felix Web Console[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--felix-web-console)

The plugin by default places an *HTTP POST* request to the [Felix Web Console](https://felix.apache.org/documentation/subprojects/apache-felix-web-console/web-console-restful-api.html#post-requests). This will achieve both upload and installation of the bundle in one request *synchronously*.

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--WebDAV_PUT"></a>WebDAV PUT[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--webdav-put)

It's also possible to use *HTTP PUT* instead of POST leveraging the [WebDAV bundle from Sling](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development). This will create a new JCR node containing the OSGi bundle in the underlying repository.
From there it needs to be picked up by the [JCR Installer](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-jcr-installer-provider) to be actually installed in the OSGi container. The latter happens *asynchronously*. It is important that the bundle resource is uploaded to a location of the repository which is actually watched by the JCR installer (by default only resources below a resource called `install`).

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Sling_POST_Servlet"></a>Sling POST Servlet[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--sling-post-servlet)

Since version 2.1.8 you can also leverage the [Sling POST servlet](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-manipulating-content-the-slingpostservlet-servlets-post) for uploading the bundle to the repository. The subsequent installation is being performed *asynchronously* by the JCR Installer (similar to the WebDAV PUT approach).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Undeploy.2FUninstall"></a>Undeploy/Uninstall[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--undeploy-uninstall)

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Felix_Web_Console"></a>Felix Web Console[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--felix-web-console-1)

Places an *HTTP POST* request to the [Felix Web Console](https://felix.apache.org/documentation/subprojects/apache-felix-web-console/web-console-restful-api.html#post-requests). This will achieve
uninstallation of the bundle *synchronously*.

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--WebDAV_PUT"></a>WebDAV PUT[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--webdav-put-1)

An *HTTP DELETE* request is issued which is handled by the [WebDAV bundle from Sling](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development). This will remove the JCR node containing the OSGi bundle in the underlying repository.
From there it needs to be picked up by the [JCR Installer](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-jcr-installer-provider) to be actually uninstalled in the OSGi container. The latter happens *asynchronously*.

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Sling_POST_Servlet"></a>Sling POST Servlet[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--sling-post-servlet-1)

An *HTTP DELETE* request is issued which is handled by the [Sling POST servlet](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-manipulating-content-the-slingpostservlet-servlets-post). This will remove the resource containing the OSGi bundle in the underlying repository. The subsequent uninstallation is being performed *asynchronously* by the JCR Installer (similar to the WebDAV PUT approach).

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--Intermediate_Resources"></a>Intermediate Resources[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-bundle-installation--intermediate-resources)

For both WebDAV PUT and Sling POST servlet installation, intermediate resources (i.e. non-existing parent resources)
are automatically created. The primary type of those intermediate nodes depend on the deployment method (only applicable if the JCR resource provider is used)

- **WebDAV PUT**, uses the configured collection node type, by default `sling:Folder` (see also [WebDAV Configuration](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development))
- **Sling POST Servlet**, uses internally `ResourceResolverFactory.create(...)` without setting any `jcr:primaryType`. Therefore the `JcrResourceProviderFactory` will call `Node.addNode(String relPath)` which determines a suitable
  node type automatically, depending on the parent's node type definition (see [JCR Node Javadoc](https://s.apache.org/jcr-2.0-javadoc/javax/jcr/Node.html#addNode(java.lang.String))).

In most of the cases the intermediate node is of type `sling:Folder`, as this is the first allowed child node definition for node type `sling:Folder`. This may only differ if your existing parent node is not of type `sling:Folder` itself.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info--plugin-documentation)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| sling:deploy | Deprecated.Use the OBR goals from themaven-bundle-plugininstead. |
| sling:deploy-file | Deprecated.Use the OBR goals from themaven-bundle-plugininstead. |
| sling:fsmount | Create OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. In case a bundle file is supplied viaAbstractFsMountMojo.bundleFileNamethe configuration for itsinitial contentis created. Otherwise it tries to detect a FileVault content package layout starting atAbstractFsMountMojo.fileVaultJcrRootFileor the project's resource directories and potentially creates a configuration for each path in the package'sfilter.xml. |
| sling:fsunmount | Remove OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. In case a bundle file is supplied viaAbstractFsMountMojo.bundleFileNamethe configuration for itsinitial contentis created. Otherwise it tries to detect a FileVault content package layout starting atAbstractFsMountMojo.fileVaultJcrRootFileor the project's resource directories and potentially creates a configuration for each path in the package'sfilter.xml. |
| sling:generate-adapter-metadata | Buildadapter metadata (JSON)for the Web Console Plugin at/system/console/status-adaptersand/system/console/adaptersfrom classes annotated withadapter annotations. |
| sling:help | Display help information on sling-maven-plugin.Callmvn sling:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| sling:install | Install the project's artifact to a running Sling instance (in case it is an OSGi bundle). It uses the first valid OSGi bundle file for deployment from the primary artifact and all secondary ones. For details refer toBundle Installation. To install an arbitrary bundle not attached to the current Maven project use goalinstall-file. |
| sling:install-file | Install an OSGi bundle from a given file path or Maven coordinates (resolved from the repository) to a running Sling instance. One of the following parameter sets are used to determine the bundle to install (evaluated in the given order):groupId,artifactId,version, and optionallyclassifierandpackagingartifactbundleFileNameTo install a bundle which has been built from the current Maven project rather use goalinstall. For details refer toBundle Installation. |
| sling:uninstall | Uninstall an OSGi bundle from a running Sling instance. For details refer toBundle Uninstallation. |
| sling:validate | Validate all JSON files of a project. It only ensures they are well-formed but not that they are valid against a certain schema. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info--system-requirements)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.3.1 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 8 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage[](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info--usage)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-2-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>  ...  <build>    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->    <pluginManagement>      <plugins>        <plugin>          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>          <artifactId>sling-maven-plugin</artifactId>          <version>3.0.2</version>        </plugin>        ...      </plugins>    </pluginManagement>    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->    <plugins>      <plugin>        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>        <artifactId>sling-maven-plugin</artifactId>        <version>3.0.2</version>      </plugin>      ...    </plugins>  </build>  ...</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation"></a>

# Bundle Installation/Uninstallation – Apache Sling Maven Plugin

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Bundle_Installation.2FUninstallation"></a>

# Bundle Installation/Uninstallation

There are three different installation approaches supported by the plugin which behave differently for the installation and uninstallation. In the following section all mechanisms are outlined individually for both use cases.

- [Bundle Installation/Uninstallation](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Bundle_Installation.2FUninstallation)
  - [Deploy/Upload/Install](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Deploy.2FUpload.2FInstall)
    - [Felix Web Console](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Felix_Web_Console)
    - [WebDAV PUT](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--WebDAV_PUT)
    - [Sling POST Servlet](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Sling_POST_Servlet)
  - [Undeploy/Uninstall](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Undeploy.2FUninstall)
    - [Felix Web Console](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Felix_Web_Console_1)
    - [WebDAV PUT](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--WebDAV_PUT_1)
    - [Sling POST Servlet](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Sling_POST_Servlet_1)
  - [Intermediate Resources](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Intermediate_Resources)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Deploy.2FUpload.2FInstall"></a>

## Deploy/Upload/Install

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Felix_Web_Console"></a>

### Felix Web Console

The plugin by default places an *HTTP POST* request to the [Felix Web Console](https://felix.apache.org/documentation/subprojects/apache-felix-web-console/web-console-restful-api.html#post-requests). This will achieve both upload and installation/update of the bundle triggered by one request. The installation/update of the bundle happens *asynchronously*, though, in the Felix Web Console.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--WebDAV_PUT"></a>

### WebDAV PUT

It's also possible to use *HTTP PUT* instead of POST leveraging the [WebDAV bundle from Sling](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development). This will create a new JCR node containing the OSGi bundle in the underlying repository.
From there it needs to be picked up by the [JCR Installer](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-jcr-installer-provider) to be actually installed in the OSGi container. The latter happens *asynchronously*. It is important that the bundle resource is uploaded to a location of the repository which is actually watched by the JCR installer (by default only resources below a resource called `install`).

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Sling_POST_Servlet"></a>

### Sling POST Servlet

Since version 2.1.8 you can also leverage the [Sling POST servlet](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-manipulating-content-the-slingpostservlet-servlets-post) for uploading the bundle to the repository. The subsequent installation is being performed *asynchronously* by the JCR Installer (similar to the WebDAV PUT approach).

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Undeploy.2FUninstall"></a>

## Undeploy/Uninstall

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Felix_Web_Console_1"></a>

### Felix Web Console

Places an *HTTP POST* request to the [Felix Web Console](https://felix.apache.org/documentation/subprojects/apache-felix-web-console/web-console-restful-api.html#post-requests). This will achieve
uninstallation of the bundle *synchronously*.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--WebDAV_PUT_1"></a>

### WebDAV PUT

An *HTTP DELETE* request is issued which is handled by the [WebDAV bundle from Sling](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development). This will remove the JCR node containing the OSGi bundle in the underlying repository.
From there it needs to be picked up by the [JCR Installer](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-jcr-installer-provider) to be actually uninstalled in the OSGi container. The latter happens *asynchronously*.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Sling_POST_Servlet_1"></a>

### Sling POST Servlet

An *HTTP DELETE* request is issued which is handled by the [Sling POST servlet](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-manipulating-content-the-slingpostservlet-servlets-post). This will remove the resource containing the OSGi bundle in the underlying repository. The subsequent uninstallation is being performed *asynchronously* by the JCR Installer (similar to the WebDAV PUT approach).

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-bundle-installation--Intermediate_Resources"></a>

## Intermediate Resources

For both WebDAV PUT and Sling POST servlet installation, intermediate resources (i.e. non-existing parent resources)
are automatically created. The primary type of those intermediate nodes depend on the deployment method (only applicable if the JCR resource provider is used)

- **WebDAV PUT**, uses the configured collection node type, by default `sling:Folder` (see also [WebDAV Configuration](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development))
- **Sling POST Servlet**, uses internally `ResourceResolverFactory.create(...)` without setting any `jcr:primaryType`. Therefore the `JcrResourceProviderFactory` will call `Node.addNode(String relPath)` which determines a suitable
  node type automatically, depending on the parent's node type definition (see [JCR Node Javadoc](https://s.apache.org/jcr-2.0-javadoc/javax/jcr/Node.html#addNode(java.lang.String))).

In most of the cases the intermediate node is of type `sling:Folder`, as this is the first allowed child node definition for node type `sling:Folder`. This may only differ if your existing parent node is not of type `sling:Folder` itself.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-plugin-info"></a>

# Plugin Documentation – Apache Sling Maven Plugin

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

# Plugin Documentation

This report describes goals, parameters details, requirements and sample usage of this plugin.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-plugin-info--Goals"></a>

## Goals

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| sling:deploy | Deprecated.Use the OBR goals from themaven-bundle-plugininstead.Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle built by maven to the OSGi Bundle Repository. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:deploy-file | Deprecated.Use the OBR goals from themaven-bundle-plugininstead.Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle referenced viasling.fileto an OSGi Bundle Repository accepting the bundle. The plugin uses amultipart/format-dataPOST request to just post the file to the URL configured in theobrproperty. |
| sling:fsmount | Create OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. In case a bundle file is supplied viabundleFileNamethe configuration for itsinitial contentis created. Otherwise it tries to detect a FileVault content package layout starting atfileVaultJcrRootFileor the project's resource directories and potentially creates a configuration for each path in the package'sfilter.xml. |
| sling:fsunmount | Remove OSGi configurations for theApache Sling File System Resource Provider. In case a bundle file is supplied viabundleFileNamethe configuration for itsinitial contentis created. Otherwise it tries to detect a FileVault content package layout starting atfileVaultJcrRootFileor the project's resource directories and potentially creates a configuration for each path in the package'sfilter.xml. |
| sling:generate-adapter-metadata | Buildadapter metadata (JSON)for the Web Console Plugin at/system/console/status-adaptersand/system/console/adaptersfrom classes annotated withadapter annotations. |
| sling:help | Display help information on sling-maven-plugin.Callmvn sling:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| sling:install | Install the project's artifact to a running Sling instance (in case it is an OSGi bundle). It uses the first valid OSGi bundle file for deployment from the primary artifact and all secondary ones. For details refer toBundle Installation. To install an arbitrary bundle not attached to the current Maven project use goalinstall-file. |
| sling:install-file | Install an OSGi bundle from a given file path or Maven coordinates (resolved from the repository) to a running Sling instance. One of the following parameter sets are used to determine the bundle to install (evaluated in the given order):groupId,artifactId,version, and optionallyclassifierandpackagingartifactbundleFileNameTo install a bundle which has been built from the current Maven project rather use goalinstall. For details refer toBundle Installation. |
| sling:uninstall | Uninstall an OSGi bundle from a running Sling instance. For details refer toBundle Uninstallation. |
| sling:validate | Validate all JSON files of a project. It only ensures they are well-formed but not that they are valid against a certain schema. |

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-archives-sling-maven-plugin-3-0-4-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

## System Requirements

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 3.8.1 |

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo"></a>

# sling:deploy-file – Apache Sling Maven Plugin

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--sling.3Adeploy-file"></a>

# sling:deploy-file

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:sling-maven-plugin:3.0.4:deploy-file

**Deprecated**:

Use the OBR goals from the [maven-bundle-plugin](https://felix.apache.org/documentation/_attachments/components/bundle-plugin/index.html) instead.

**Description**:

Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle referenced via `sling.file` to an OSGi Bundle Repository accepting the bundle. The plugin uses a *multipart/format-data* POST request to just post the file to the URL configured in the `obr` property.

**Attributes**:

- The goal is not marked as thread-safe and thus does not support parallel builds.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--Required_Parameters"></a>

## Required Parameters

| Name | Type | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <obr> | String | - | The URL to the OSGi Bundle repository to which the bundle is posted, e.g.http://obr.sample.comUser Property:obr |
| <slingUrl> | URI | - | The URL of the running Sling instance.The default is only useful forWebConsoledeployment.ForWebDAVdeployment it is recommended to include theSling Simple WebDAV servlet root, for instancehttp://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install. Omitting thedav/defaultsegment can lead to conflicts with other servlets.Default:http://localhost:8080/system/consoleUser Property:sling.url |

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--Optional_Parameters"></a>

## Optional Parameters

| Name | Type | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <bundleFileName> | String | - | The name of the generated JAR file.User Property:sling.file |
| <failOnError> | boolean | - | Determines whether or not to fail the build if the HTTP POST or PUT returns an non-OK response code.Default:trueUser Property:sling.failOnError |
| <httpConnectTimeoutSec> | int | 3.0.0 | HTTP connection timeout (in seconds). Determines the timeout until a new connection is fully established. This may also include transport security negotiation exchanges such asSSLorTLSprotocol negotiation).Default:10User Property:sling.httpConnectTimeoutSec |
| <httpResponseTimeoutSec> | int | 3.0.0 | HTTP response timeout (in seconds). Determines the timeout until arrival of a response from the opposite endpoint.Default:60User Property:sling.httpResponseTimeoutSec |
| <password> | String | - | The password to authenticate at the running Sling instance.Default:adminUser Property:sling.password |
| <slingConsoleUrl> | URI | - | The WebConsole URL of the running Sling instance. This is required for file system provider operations. If not configured the value of slingUrl is used.User Property:sling.console.url |
| <slingUrlSuffix> | String | - | An optional url suffix which will be appended to thesling.urlfor use as the real target url. This allows to configure different target URLs in each POM, while using the same commonsling.urlin a parent POM (eg.sling.url=http://localhost:8080andsling.urlSuffix=/project/specific/path). This is typically used in conjunction with WebDAV or SlingPostServlet deployment methods.User Property:sling.urlSuffix |
| <user> | String | - | The user name to authenticate at the running Sling instance.Default:adminUser Property:sling.user |

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--failOnError"></a>

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`

- **Default**: `true`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--httpConnectTimeoutSec"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--a.3ChttpConnectTimeoutSec.3E"></a>

### <httpConnectTimeoutSec>

HTTP connection timeout (in seconds). Determines the timeout until a new connection is fully established. This may also include transport security negotiation exchanges such as `SSL` or `TLS` protocol negotiation).

- **Type**: `int`
- **Since**: `3.0.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.httpConnectTimeoutSec`
- **Default**: `10`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--httpResponseTimeoutSec"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--a.3ChttpResponseTimeoutSec.3E"></a>

### <httpResponseTimeoutSec>

HTTP response timeout (in seconds). Determines the timeout until arrival of a response from the opposite endpoint.

- **Type**: `int`
- **Since**: `3.0.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.httpResponseTimeoutSec`
- **Default**: `60`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--obr"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--a.3Cobr.3E"></a>

### <obr>

The URL to the OSGi Bundle repository to which the bundle is posted, e.g. `http://obr.sample.com`

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `Yes`
- **User Property**: `obr`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--password"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--a.3Cpassword.3E"></a>

### <password>

The password to authenticate at the running Sling instance.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.password`
- **Default**: `admin`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--slingConsoleUrl"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--a.3CslingConsoleUrl.3E"></a>

### <slingConsoleUrl>

The WebConsole URL of the running Sling instance. This is required for file system provider operations. If not configured the value of slingUrl is used.

- **Type**: `java.net.URI`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.console.url`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--slingUrl"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--a.3CslingUrl.3E"></a>

### <slingUrl>

The URL of the running Sling instance.

The default is only useful for **WebConsole** deployment.

For **WebDAV** deployment it is recommended to include the [Sling Simple WebDAV servlet root](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development--separate-uri-space-webdav), for instance [http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install](http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install). Omitting the `dav/default` segment can lead to conflicts with other servlets.

- **Type**: `java.net.URI`
- **Required**: `Yes`
- **User Property**: `sling.url`
- **Default**: `http://localhost:8080/system/console`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--slingUrlSuffix"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--a.3CslingUrlSuffix.3E"></a>

### <slingUrlSuffix>

An optional url suffix which will be appended to the `sling.url` for use as the real target url. This allows to configure different target URLs in each POM, while using the same common `sling.url` in a parent POM (eg. `sling.url=http://localhost:8080` and `sling.urlSuffix=/project/specific/path`). This is typically used in conjunction with WebDAV or SlingPostServlet deployment methods.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.urlSuffix`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--user"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-file-mojo--a.3Cuser.3E"></a>

### <user>

The user name to authenticate at the running Sling instance.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.user`
- **Default**: `admin`

---

# sling:deploy

**Full name**:

**Deprecated**:

Use the OBR goals from the [maven-bundle-plugin](https://felix.apache.org/documentation/_attachments/components/bundle-plugin/index.html) instead.

**Description**:

Deploy a JAR representing an OSGi Bundle to a Sling OSGi Bundle Repository. This method posts the bundle built by maven to the OSGi Bundle Repository. The plugin uses a *multipart/format-data* POST request to just post the file to the URL configured in the `obr` property.

**Attributes**:

- Requires a Maven project to be executed.
- The goal is not marked as thread-safe and thus does not support parallel builds.
- Binds by default to the [lifecycle phase](https://maven.apache.org/ref/current/maven-core/lifecycles.html): `deploy`.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-mojo--a.3Cskip.3E"></a>

### <skip>

Whether to skip this step even though it has been configured in the project to be executed. This property may be set by the `sling.deploy.skip` comparable to the `maven.test.skip` property to prevent running the unit tests.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `Yes`
- **User Property**: `sling.deploy.skip`
- **Default**: `false`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-mojo--slingConsoleUrl"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-mojo--a.3CslingConsoleUrl.3E"></a>

### <slingConsoleUrl>

The WebConsole URL of the running Sling instance. This is required for file system provider operations. If not configured the value of slingUrl is used.

- **Type**: `java.net.URI`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.console.url`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-mojo--slingUrl"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-mojo--a.3CslingUrl.3E"></a>

### <slingUrl>

The URL of the running Sling instance.

The default is only useful for **WebConsole** deployment.

For **WebDAV** deployment it is recommended to include the [Sling Simple WebDAV servlet root](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development--separate-uri-space-webdav), for instance [http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install](http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install). Omitting the `dav/default` segment can lead to conflicts with other servlets.

- **Type**: `java.net.URI`
- **Required**: `Yes`
- **User Property**: `sling.url`
- **Default**: `http://localhost:8080/system/console`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-mojo--slingUrlSuffix"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-mojo--a.3CslingUrlSuffix.3E"></a>

### <slingUrlSuffix>

An optional url suffix which will be appended to the `sling.url` for use as the real target url. This allows to configure different target URLs in each POM, while using the same common `sling.url` in a parent POM (eg. `sling.url=http://localhost:8080` and `sling.urlSuffix=/project/specific/path`). This is typically used in conjunction with WebDAV or SlingPostServlet deployment methods.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.urlSuffix`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-mojo--user"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-deploy-mojo--a.3Cuser.3E"></a>

### <user>

The user name to authenticate at the running Sling instance.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.user`
- **Default**: `admin`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-fsmount-mojo"></a>

# sling:fsmount – Apache Sling Maven Plugin

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-fsmount-mojo--sling.3Afsmount"></a>

# sling:fsmount

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:sling-maven-plugin:3.0.4:fsmount

**Description**:

Create OSGi configurations for the [Apache Sling File System Resource Provider](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-accessing-filesystem-resources-extensions-fsresource). In case a bundle file is supplied via `bundleFileName` the configuration for its [initial content](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-content-loading-jcr-contentloader--initial-content-loading) is created. Otherwise it tries to detect a FileVault content package layout starting at `fileVaultJcrRootFile` or the project's resource directories and potentially creates a configuration for each path in the package's `filter.xml`.

**Attributes**:

- Requires a Maven project to be executed.
- The goal is not marked as thread-safe and thus does not support parallel builds.
- Since version: `2.2.0`.

Omitting thedav/defaultsegment can lead to conflicts with other servlets.Default:http://localhost:8080/system/consoleUser Property:sling.url |

### <deployFsResourceBundlePrerequisites>

Bundles that have to be installed as prerequisites to execute this goal. With multiple entries in the list different bundles with different preconditions can be defined.
  
**Default value is:**:

```xml
<deployFsResourceBundlePrerequisites>
  <bundlePrerequisite>
    <bundles>
      <bundle>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>org.apache.sling.fsresource</artifactId>
        <version>2.3.0</version>
      </bundle>
    </bundles>
    <preconditions>
      <bundle>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>org.apache.sling.commons.johnzon</artifactId>
        <version>2.0.0</version>
      </bundle>
      <bundle>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>org.apache.sling.api</artifactId>
        <version>2.25.4</version>
      </bundle>
      <bundle>
        <groupId>org.apache.commons</groupId>
        <artifactId>commons-collections4</artifactId>
        <version>4.1</version>
        <symbolicName>org.apache.commons.collections4</symbolicName>
      </bundle>
    </preconditions>
  </bundlePrerequisite>
  <bundlePrerequisite>
    <bundles>
      <bundle>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>org.apache.sling.commons.johnzon</artifactId>
        <version>1.2.6</version>
      </bundle>
      <bundle>
        <groupId>org.apache.commons</groupId>
        <artifactId>commons-collections4</artifactId>
        <version>4.1</version>
        <symbolicName>org.apache.commons.collections4</symbolicName>
      </bundle>
      <bundle>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>org.apache.sling.fsresource</artifactId>
        <version>2.2.0</version>
      </bundle>
    </bundles>
    <preconditions>
      <bundle>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>org.apache.sling.resourceresolver</artifactId>
        <version>1.5.18</version>
      </bundle>
    </preconditions>
  </bundlePrerequisite>
  <bundlePrerequisite>
    <bundles>
      <bundle>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>org.apache.sling.fsresource</artifactId>
        <version>1.4.8</version>
      </bundle>
    </bundles>
  </bundlePrerequisite>
</deployFsResourceBundlePrerequisites>
```

- **Type**: `java.util.List<org.apache.sling.maven.bundlesupport.BundlePrerequisite>`

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-fsmount-mojo--deploymentMethod"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-fsmount-mojo--a.3CdeploymentMethod.3E"></a>

### <deploymentMethod>

Bundle deployment method. One of the following three values are allowed

1. **WebConsole**, uses the [ Felix Web Console REST API](http://felix.apache.org/documentation/subprojects/apache-felix-web-console/web-console-restful-api.html#post-requests) for deployment (HTTP POST). This is the default. Make sure that `slingUrl` points to the Felix Web Console in that case.
2. **WebDAV**, uses [ WebDAV](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development) for deployment (HTTP PUT). Make sure that `slingUrl` points to the entry path of the Sling WebDAV bundle (defaults to `/dav/default` in the Sling starter). Issues a HTTP Delete for the uninstall goal.
3. **SlingPostServlet**, uses the [Sling Post Servlet](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-manipulating-content-the-slingpostservlet-servlets-post) for deployment (HTTP POST). Make sure that `slingUrl` points a path which is handled by the Sling POST Servlet (usually below regular Sling root URL).

For more details refer to [Bundle Installation](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-bundle-installation).

- **Type**: `org.apache.sling.maven.bundlesupport.deploy.BundleDeploymentMethod`
- **Since**: `2.3.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.deploy.method`
- **Default**: `WebConsole`

---

# sling:fsunmount

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:sling-maven-plugin:3.0.4:fsunmount

**Description**:

Remove OSGi configurations for the [Apache Sling File System Resource Provider](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-accessing-filesystem-resources-extensions-fsresource). In case a bundle file is supplied via `bundleFileName` the configuration for its [initial content](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-content-loading-jcr-contentloader--initial-content-loading) is created. Otherwise it tries to detect a FileVault content package layout starting at `fileVaultJcrRootFile` or the project's resource directories and potentially creates a configuration for each path in the package's `filter.xml`.

**Attributes**:

- Requires a Maven project to be executed.
- The goal is not marked as thread-safe and thus does not support parallel builds.
- Since version: `2.2.0`.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-fsunmount-mojo--slingUrl"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-fsunmount-mojo--a.3CslingUrl.3E"></a>

### <slingUrl>

The URL of the running Sling instance.

The default is only useful for **WebConsole** deployment.

For **WebDAV** deployment it is recommended to include the [Sling Simple WebDAV servlet root](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development--separate-uri-space-webdav), for instance [http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install](http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install). Omitting the `dav/default` segment can lead to conflicts with other servlets.

- **Type**: `java.net.URI`
- **Required**: `Yes`
- **User Property**: `sling.url`
- **Default**: `http://localhost:8080/system/console`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-fsunmount-mojo--slingUrlSuffix"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-fsunmount-mojo--a.3CslingUrlSuffix.3E"></a>

### <slingUrlSuffix>

An optional url suffix which will be appended to the `sling.url` for use as the real target url. This allows to configure different target URLs in each POM, while using the same common `sling.url` in a parent POM (eg. `sling.url=http://localhost:8080` and `sling.urlSuffix=/project/specific/path`). This is typically used in conjunction with WebDAV or SlingPostServlet deployment methods.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.urlSuffix`

---

- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.user`
- **Default**: `admin`

---

# sling:help

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:sling-maven-plugin:3.0.4:help

**Description**:

Display help information on sling-maven-plugin.
  
Call `mvn sling:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>` to display parameter details.

**Attributes**:

- The goal is thread-safe and supports parallel builds.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-help-mojo--Optional_Parameters"></a>

| <goal> | String | - | The name of the goal for which to show help. If unspecified, all goals will be displayed.User Property:goal |
| <indentSize> | int | - | The number of spaces per indentation level, should be positive.Default:2User Property:indentSize |
| <lineLength> | int | - | The maximum length of a display line, should be positive.Default:80User Property:lineLength |

# sling:install-file – Apache Sling Maven Plugin

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--sling.3Ainstall-file"></a>

# sling:install-file

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:sling-maven-plugin:3.0.4:install-file

**Description**:

Install an OSGi bundle from a given file path or Maven coordinates (resolved from the repository) to a running Sling instance. One of the following parameter sets are used to determine the bundle to install (evaluated in the given order):

- `groupId`, `artifactId`, `version`, and optionally `classifier` and `packaging`
- `artifact`
- `bundleFileName`

To install a bundle which has been built from the current Maven project rather use goal install. For details refer to [Bundle Installation](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-bundle-installation).

**Attributes**:

- The goal is not marked as thread-safe and thus does not support parallel builds.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--Required_Parameters"></a>

## Required Parameters

| Name | Type | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <slingUrl> | URI | - | The URL of the running Sling instance.The default is only useful forWebConsoledeployment.ForWebDAVdeployment it is recommended to include theSling Simple WebDAV servlet root, for instancehttp://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install. Omitting thedav/defaultsegment can lead to conflicts with other servlets.Default:http://localhost:8080/system/consoleUser Property:sling.url |

| <artifactId> | String | - | The artifactId of the artifact to install. Takes precedence overartifactandbundleFileName.User Property:sling.artifactId |
| <bundleFileName> | File | - | The path of the bundle file to install. Is only effective if artifact is not determined via some other way (Maven coordinates).Default:${project.build.directory}/${project.build.finalName}.jarUser Property:sling.file |
| <bundleStart> | boolean | - | Whether to start the uploaded bundle or not. Only applies when POSTing to Felix Web ConsoleDefault:trueUser Property:sling.bundle.start |

The parameter is also ignored if the running Sling instance has no StartLevel service (which is unusual actually). Only applies when POSTing to Felix Web Console.Default:20User Property:sling.bundle.startlevel |
| <classifier> | String | - | The classifier of the artifact to installUser Property:sling.classifier |
| <deploymentMethod> | BundleDeploymentMethod | - | Bundle deployment method. One of the following three values are allowedWebConsole, uses theFelix Web Console REST APIfor deployment (HTTP POST). This is the default. Make sure thatslingUrlpoints to the Felix Web Console in that case.WebDAV, usesWebDAVfor deployment (HTTP PUT). Make sure thatslingUrlpoints to the entry path of the Sling WebDAV bundle (defaults to/dav/defaultin the Sling starter). Issues a HTTP Delete for the uninstall goal.SlingPostServlet, uses theSling Post Servletfor deployment (HTTP POST). Make sure thatslingUrlpoints a path which is handled by the Sling POST Servlet (usually below regular Sling root URL).For more details refer toBundle Installation. This has precedence over the deprecated parameterusePut. If nothing is set the default is eitherWebConsoleorWebDAV(whenusePutistrue).User Property:sling.deploy.method |

| <groupId> | String | - | The groupId of the artifact to install. Takes precedence overartifactandbundleFileName.User Property:sling.groupId |
| <httpConnectTimeoutSec> | int | 3.0.0 | HTTP connection timeout (in seconds). Determines the timeout until a new connection is fully established. This may also include transport security negotiation exchanges such asSSLorTLSprotocol negotiation).Default:10User Property:sling.httpConnectTimeoutSec |
| <httpResponseTimeoutSec> | int | 3.0.0 | HTTP response timeout (in seconds). Determines the timeout until arrival of a response from the opposite endpoint.Default:60User Property:sling.httpResponseTimeoutSec |
| <mimeType> | String | - | The content type / mime type used for WebDAV or Sling POST deployment.Default:application/java-archiveUser Property:sling.mimeType |
| <mountByFS> | boolean | - | Whether to add (for install)/remove (for uninstall) the mapping for theApache Sling File System Resource Providerfor thebundle's initial content. This parameter must not betruewith bundles resolved from the Maven repository.Default:falseUser Property:sling.mountByFS |

This allows to configure different target URLs in each POM, while using the same commonsling.urlin a parent POM (eg.sling.url=http://localhost:8080andsling.urlSuffix=/project/specific/path). This is typically used in conjunction with WebDAV or SlingPostServlet deployment methods.User Property:sling.urlSuffix |

## Parameter Details

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--artifact"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--a.3Cartifact.3E"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--artifactId"></a>

- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.file`

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--a.3CbundleStart.3E"></a>

### <bundleStart>

Whether to start the uploaded bundle or not. Only applies when POSTing to Felix Web Console

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.bundle.start`
- **Default**: `true`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--bundleStartLevel"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--a.3CbundleStartLevel.3E"></a>

### <bundleStartLevel>

The start level to set on the installed bundle. If the bundle is already installed and therefore is only updated this parameter is ignored. The parameter is also ignored if the running Sling instance has no StartLevel service (which is unusual actually). Only applies when POSTing to Felix Web Console.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.bundle.startlevel`
- **Default**: `20`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--classifier"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--a.3Cclassifier.3E"></a>

The classifier of the artifact to install

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.classifier`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--deploymentMethod"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--a.3CdeploymentMethod.3E"></a>

### <deploymentMethod>

Bundle deployment method. One of the following three values are allowed

1. **WebConsole**, uses the [ Felix Web Console REST API](http://felix.apache.org/documentation/subprojects/apache-felix-web-console/web-console-restful-api.html#post-requests) for deployment (HTTP POST). This is the default. Make sure that `slingUrl` points to the Felix Web Console in that case.
2. **WebDAV**, uses [ WebDAV](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development) for deployment (HTTP PUT). Make sure that `slingUrl` points to the entry path of the Sling WebDAV bundle (defaults to `/dav/default` in the Sling starter). Issues a HTTP Delete for the uninstall goal.
3. **SlingPostServlet**, uses the [Sling Post Servlet](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-manipulating-content-the-slingpostservlet-servlets-post) for deployment (HTTP POST). Make sure that `slingUrl` points a path which is handled by the Sling POST Servlet (usually below regular Sling root URL).

For more details refer to [Bundle Installation](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-bundle-installation). This has precedence over the deprecated parameter `usePut`. If nothing is set the default is either `WebConsole` or `WebDAV` (when `usePut` is `true`).

- **Type**: `org.apache.sling.maven.bundlesupport.deploy.BundleDeploymentMethod`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.deploy.method`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-file-mojo--a.3CfailOnError.3E"></a>

- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.failOnError`
- **Default**: `true`

---

### <slingUrlSuffix>

An optional url suffix which will be appended to the `sling.url` for use as the real target url. This allows to configure different target URLs in each POM, while using the same common `sling.url` in a parent POM (eg. `sling.url=http://localhost:8080` and `sling.urlSuffix=/project/specific/path`). This is typically used in conjunction with WebDAV or SlingPostServlet deployment methods.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.urlSuffix`

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo"></a>

# sling:install – Apache Sling Maven Plugin

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo--sling.3Ainstall"></a>

# sling:install

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:sling-maven-plugin:3.0.4:install

**Description**:

Install the project's artifact to a running Sling instance (in case it is an OSGi bundle). It uses the first valid OSGi bundle file for deployment from the primary artifact and all secondary ones. For details refer to [Bundle Installation](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-bundle-installation). To install an arbitrary bundle not attached to the current Maven project use goal install-file.

**Attributes**:

- Requires a Maven project to be executed.
- The goal is not marked as thread-safe and thus does not support parallel builds.
- Binds by default to the [lifecycle phase](https://maven.apache.org/ref/current/maven-core/lifecycles.html): `install`.

Omitting thedav/defaultsegment can lead to conflicts with other servlets.Default:http://localhost:8080/system/consoleUser Property:sling.url |

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo--Parameter_Details"></a>

## Parameter Details

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo--bundleStart"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo--a.3CbundleStart.3E"></a>

### <bundleStart>

Whether to start the uploaded bundle or not. Only applies when POSTing to Felix Web Console

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.bundle.start`
- **Default**: `true`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo--bundleStartLevel"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo--a.3CbundleStartLevel.3E"></a>

### <bundleStartLevel>

The start level to set on the installed bundle. If the bundle is already installed and therefore is only updated this parameter is ignored. The parameter is also ignored if the running Sling instance has no StartLevel service (which is unusual actually). Only applies when POSTing to Felix Web Console.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.bundle.startlevel`
- **Default**: `20`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo--deploymentMethod"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo--a.3CdeploymentMethod.3E"></a>

### <deploymentMethod>

Bundle deployment method. One of the following three values are allowed

1. **WebConsole**, uses the [ Felix Web Console REST API](http://felix.apache.org/documentation/subprojects/apache-felix-web-console/web-console-restful-api.html#post-requests) for deployment (HTTP POST). This is the default. Make sure that `slingUrl` points to the Felix Web Console in that case.
2. **WebDAV**, uses [ WebDAV](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development) for deployment (HTTP PUT). Make sure that `slingUrl` points to the entry path of the Sling WebDAV bundle (defaults to `/dav/default` in the Sling starter). Issues a HTTP Delete for the uninstall goal.
3. **SlingPostServlet**, uses the [Sling Post Servlet](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-manipulating-content-the-slingpostservlet-servlets-post) for deployment (HTTP POST). Make sure that `slingUrl` points a path which is handled by the Sling POST Servlet (usually below regular Sling root URL).

For more details refer to [Bundle Installation](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-bundle-installation). This has precedence over the deprecated parameter `usePut`. If nothing is set the default is either `WebConsole` or `WebDAV` (when `usePut` is `true`).

- **Type**: `org.apache.sling.maven.bundlesupport.deploy.BundleDeploymentMethod`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.deploy.method`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-install-mojo--a.3CfailOnError.3E"></a>

- **Default**: `true`

### <slingUrl>

The default is only useful for **WebConsole** deployment.

For **WebDAV** deployment it is recommended to include the [Sling Simple WebDAV servlet root](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development--separate-uri-space-webdav), for instance [http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install](http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install). Omitting the `dav/default` segment can lead to conflicts with other servlets.

- **Required**: `Yes`
- **User Property**: `sling.url`
- **Default**: `http://localhost:8080/system/console`

---

This is typically used in conjunction with WebDAV or SlingPostServlet deployment methods.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.urlSuffix`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--Parameter_Details"></a>

## Parameter Details

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--bundleFileName"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CbundleFileName.3E"></a>

### <bundleFileName>

**Deprecated.**  
Use `bundleName` instead

  

The path of bundle file to uninstall. The file is only used to determine the file name or bundle symbolic name. This parameter is only effective if `bundleName` is not set.

- **Type**: `java.io.File`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.file`
- **Default**: `${project.build.directory}/${project.build.finalName}.jar`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--bundleName"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CbundleName.3E"></a>

### <bundleName>

The bundles's file/resource name without path (for all `deploymentMethod`s except for `WebConsole`) or its symbolic name. If this parameter is set, it takes precedence over `bundleFileName`.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.bundle.name`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--bundleStart"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CbundleStart.3E"></a>

### <bundleStart>

Whether to start the uploaded bundle or not. Only applies when POSTing to Felix Web Console

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.bundle.start`
- **Default**: `true`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--bundleStartLevel"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CbundleStartLevel.3E"></a>

### <bundleStartLevel>

The start level to set on the installed bundle. If the bundle is already installed and therefore is only updated this parameter is ignored. The parameter is also ignored if the running Sling instance has no StartLevel service (which is unusual actually). Only applies when POSTing to Felix Web Console.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.bundle.startlevel`
- **Default**: `20`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--deploymentMethod"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CdeploymentMethod.3E"></a>

### <deploymentMethod>

Bundle deployment method. One of the following three values are allowed

1. **WebConsole**, uses the [ Felix Web Console REST API](http://felix.apache.org/documentation/subprojects/apache-felix-web-console/web-console-restful-api.html#post-requests) for deployment (HTTP POST). This is the default. Make sure that `slingUrl` points to the Felix Web Console in that case.
2. **WebDAV**, uses [ WebDAV](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development) for deployment (HTTP PUT). Make sure that `slingUrl` points to the entry path of the Sling WebDAV bundle (defaults to `/dav/default` in the Sling starter). Issues a HTTP Delete for the uninstall goal.
3. **SlingPostServlet**, uses the [Sling Post Servlet](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-manipulating-content-the-slingpostservlet-servlets-post) for deployment (HTTP POST). Make sure that `slingUrl` points a path which is handled by the Sling POST Servlet (usually below regular Sling root URL).

For more details refer to [Bundle Installation](#sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-bundle-installation). This has precedence over the deprecated parameter `usePut`. If nothing is set the default is either `WebConsole` or `WebDAV` (when `usePut` is `true`).

- **Type**: `org.apache.sling.maven.bundlesupport.deploy.BundleDeploymentMethod`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.deploy.method`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--failOnError"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CfailOnError.3E"></a>

### <failOnError>

Determines whether or not to fail the build if the HTTP POST or PUT returns an non-OK response code.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.failOnError`
- **Default**: `true`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--httpConnectTimeoutSec"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3ChttpConnectTimeoutSec.3E"></a>

### <httpConnectTimeoutSec>

HTTP connection timeout (in seconds). Determines the timeout until a new connection is fully established. This may also include transport security negotiation exchanges such as `SSL` or `TLS` protocol negotiation).

- **Type**: `int`
- **Since**: `3.0.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.httpConnectTimeoutSec`
- **Default**: `10`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--httpResponseTimeoutSec"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3ChttpResponseTimeoutSec.3E"></a>

### <httpResponseTimeoutSec>

HTTP response timeout (in seconds). Determines the timeout until arrival of a response from the opposite endpoint.

- **Type**: `int`
- **Since**: `3.0.0`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.httpResponseTimeoutSec`
- **Default**: `60`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--mimeType"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CmimeType.3E"></a>

### <mimeType>

The content type / mime type used for WebDAV or Sling POST deployment.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.mimeType`
- **Default**: `application/java-archive`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--mountByFS"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CmountByFS.3E"></a>

### <mountByFS>

Whether to add (for install)/remove (for uninstall) the mapping for the [Apache Sling File System Resource Provider](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-accessing-filesystem-resources-extensions-fsresource) for the [bundle's initial content](#sling-apache-org-documentation-bundles-content-loading-jcr-contentloader--initial-content-loading). This parameter must not be `true` with bundles resolved from the Maven repository.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.mountByFS`
- **Default**: `false`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--password"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3Cpassword.3E"></a>

### <password>

The password to authenticate at the running Sling instance.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.password`
- **Default**: `admin`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--refreshPackages"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CrefreshPackages.3E"></a>

### <refreshPackages>

Whether to refresh the packages after installing the uploaded bundle. Only applies when POSTing to Felix Web Console

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.refreshPackages`
- **Default**: `true`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--slingConsoleUrl"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CslingConsoleUrl.3E"></a>

### <slingConsoleUrl>

The WebConsole URL of the running Sling instance. This is required for file system provider operations. If not configured the value of slingUrl is used.

- **Type**: `java.net.URI`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.console.url`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--slingUrl"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CslingUrl.3E"></a>

### <slingUrl>

The URL of the running Sling instance.

The default is only useful for **WebConsole** deployment.

For **WebDAV** deployment it is recommended to include the [Sling Simple WebDAV servlet root](#sling-apache-org-documentation-development-repository-based-development--separate-uri-space-webdav), for instance [http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install](http://localhost:8080/dav/default/libs/sling/install). Omitting the `dav/default` segment can lead to conflicts with other servlets.

- **Type**: `java.net.URI`
- **Required**: `Yes`
- **User Property**: `sling.url`
- **Default**: `http://localhost:8080/system/console`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--slingUrlSuffix"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CslingUrlSuffix.3E"></a>

### <slingUrlSuffix>

An optional url suffix which will be appended to the `sling.url` for use as the real target url. This allows to configure different target URLs in each POM, while using the same common `sling.url` in a parent POM (eg. `sling.url=http://localhost:8080` and `sling.urlSuffix=/project/specific/path`). This is typically used in conjunction with WebDAV or SlingPostServlet deployment methods.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.urlSuffix`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--usePut"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3CusePut.3E"></a>

### <usePut>

**Deprecated.**  
Use `deploymentMethod` instead.

  

If a PUT via WebDAV should be used instead of the standard POST to the Felix Web Console. In the `uninstall` goal, a HTTP DELETE will be used.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.usePut`
- **Default**: `false`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--user"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-uninstall-mojo--a.3Cuser.3E"></a>

### <user>

The user name to authenticate at the running Sling instance.

- **Type**: `java.lang.String`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.user`
- **Default**: `admin`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo"></a>

# sling:validate – Apache Sling Maven Plugin

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo--sling.3Avalidate"></a>

# sling:validate

**Full name**:

org.apache.sling:sling-maven-plugin:3.0.4:validate

**Description**:

Validate all JSON files of a project. It only ensures they are well-formed but not that they are valid against a certain schema.

**Attributes**:

- Requires a Maven project to be executed.
- The goal is thread-safe and supports parallel builds.
- Binds by default to the [lifecycle phase](https://maven.apache.org/ref/current/maven-core/lifecycles.html): `process-resources`.

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo--Optional_Parameters"></a>

## Optional Parameters

| Name | Type | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <jsonQuoteTick> | boolean | - | Whether to accept quote ticks in JSON files or not.Default:falseUser Property:sling.validation.jsonQuoteTick |
| <skip> | boolean | - | Whether to skip the validation.Default:falseUser Property:sling.validation.skip |
| <skipJson> | boolean | - | Whether to skip the json validation. At the time, there's no difference betweenskipandskipJsonbecause only JSON files will be validated by now.Default:falseUser Property:sling.validation.skipJson |

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo--Parameter_Details"></a>

## Parameter Details

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo--jsonQuoteTick"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo--a.3CjsonQuoteTick.3E"></a>

### <jsonQuoteTick>

Whether to accept quote ticks in JSON files or not.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.validation.jsonQuoteTick`
- **Default**: `false`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo--skip"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo--a.3Cskip.3E"></a>

### <skip>

Whether to skip the validation.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.validation.skip`
- **Default**: `false`

---

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo--skipJson"></a>

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-sling-maven-plugin-validate-mojo--a.3CskipJson.3E"></a>

### <skipJson>

Whether to skip the json validation. At the time, there's no difference between `skip` and `skipJson` because only JSON files will be validated by now.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Required**: `No`
- **User Property**: `sling.validation.skipJson`
- **Default**: `false`

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-1-20-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling OSGi Feature Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-1-20-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-1-20-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| slingfeature:aggregate-features | Aggregate multiple features into a single one. |
| slingfeature:analyse-features | Analyse the feature. |
| slingfeature:apis-jar | Generates the APIs JARs for each selected Feature file. |
| slingfeature:attach-featurearchives | Create a feature model archive and attach it. An archive is created for each feature of this project |
| slingfeature:attach-features | Attach the feature as a project artifact. |
| slingfeature:collect-artifacts | No description. |
| slingfeature:embed-features | Embed the features in the resources |
| slingfeature:extract-extension | No description. |
| slingfeature:features-diff | Compares different versions of the same Feature Model. |
| slingfeature:help | Display help information on slingfeature-maven-plugin.Callmvn slingfeature:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| slingfeature:include-artifact | This goal creates a Feature Model file that includes the Module Artifact as bundle (or extension) so that the Artifact can be added through a FM into a FM project. The FM file can be found in the 'build directory'/slingfeature-tmp folder. After a FM file is created successfully this file will be installed in the local Maven Repository as 'slingosgifeature' file under the Module's Maven Id location (group, artifact, version). This file can then later be used inside the 'aggregate-features' goal with:<includeArtifact> <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId> <artifactId>org.apache.sling.test.feature</artifactId> <version>1.0.0</version> <classifier>my-test-classifier</classifier> <type>slingosgifeature</type> </includeArtifact>It also can add dependencies to the FM file if its scope is provided (normally that would be 'compile'). In addition a bundle start order can be set for these included dependency bundles. Finally any FM files inside the Source FM folder are embedded into the FM file. This allows to add extension files like 'repoinit' etc to be added to provide them with the module. |
| slingfeature:info | Extract information from a feature This mojo does not require a project, it can be run by just pointing it at a feature file. When run from within a project, the normal feature selection mechanism can be used. This mojo supportsExtracting the exported packages per feature and writing them to a fileDetecting duplicates across features and writing a report |
| slingfeature:launch-features | Launches the given Feature File |
| slingfeature:repository | Create a Maven repository structure from the referenced artifacts in the features. |
| slingfeature:update-feature-versions | Update the bundles/artifact versions |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-1-20-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-1-20-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.8 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-1-20-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-1-20-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>slingfeature-maven-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>1.1.20</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>slingfeature-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>1.1.20</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-2-0-plugin-info"></a>

# Apache Sling OSGi Feature Maven Plugin – Plugin Documentation

## <a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-2-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>Plugin Documentation

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-2-0-plugin-info--Plugin_Documentation"></a>

Goals available for this plugin:

| Goal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| slingfeature:aggregate-features | Aggregate multiple features into a single one. |
| slingfeature:analyse-features | Analyse the feature. |
| slingfeature:apis-jar | Generates the APIs JARs for the selected feature files. |
| slingfeature:attach-featurearchives | Create a feature model archive and attach it. An archive is created for each feature of this project |
| slingfeature:attach-features | Attach the feature as a project artifact. |
| slingfeature:collect-artifacts | No description. |
| slingfeature:embed-features | Embed the features in the resources |
| slingfeature:extract-extension | No description. |
| slingfeature:features-diff | Compares different versions of the same Feature Model. |
| slingfeature:help | Display help information on slingfeature-maven-plugin.Callmvn slingfeature:help -Ddetail=true -Dgoal=<goal-name>to display parameter details. |
| slingfeature:include-artifact | This goal creates a Feature Model file that includes the Module Artifact as bundle (or extension) so that the Artifact can be added through a FM into a FM project. The FM file can be found in the 'build directory'/slingfeature-tmp folder. After a FM file is created successfully this file will be installed in the local Maven Repository as 'slingosgifeature' file under the Module's Maven Id location (group, artifact, version). This file can then later be used inside the 'aggregate-features' goal with:<includeArtifact> <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId> <artifactId>org.apache.sling.test.feature</artifactId> <version>1.0.0</version> <classifier>my-test-classifier</classifier> <type>slingosgifeature</type> </includeArtifact>It also can add dependencies to the FM file if its scope is provided (normally that would be 'compile'). In addition a bundle start order can be set for these included dependency bundles. Finally any FM files inside the Source FM folder are embedded into the FM file. This allows to add extension files like 'repoinit' etc to be added to provide them with the module. |
| slingfeature:info | Extract information from a feature This mojo does not require a project, it can be run by just pointing it at a feature file. When run from within a project, the normal feature selection mechanism can be used. This mojo supportsExtracting the exported packages per feature and writing them to a fileDetecting duplicates across features and writing a report |
| slingfeature:launch-features | Launches the given Feature File |
| slingfeature:repository | Create a Maven repository structure from the referenced artifacts in the features. |
| slingfeature:update-feature-versions | Update the bundles/artifact versions |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-2-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>System Requirements

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-2-0-plugin-info--System_Requirements"></a>

The following specifies the minimum requirements to run this Maven plugin:

| Maven | 2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| JDK | 1.8 |
| Memory | No minimum requirement. |
| Disk Space | No minimum requirement. |

### <a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-2-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>Usage

<a id="sling-apache-org-components-slingfeature-maven-plugin-archives-slingfeature-maven-plugin-1-2-0-plugin-info--Usage"></a>

You should specify the version in your project's plugin configuration:

```xml
<project>
  ...
  <build>
    <!-- To define the plugin version in your parent POM -->
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
          <artifactId>slingfeature-maven-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>1.2.0</version>
        </plugin>
        ...
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
    <!-- To use the plugin goals in your POM or parent POM -->
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.sling</groupId>
        <artifactId>slingfeature-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>1.2.0</version>
      </plugin>
      ...
    </plugins>
  </build>
  ...
</project>
```

For more information, see ["Guide to Configuring Plug-ins"](http://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-configuring-plugins.html)
